#!/bin/bash
# Run cargo against one crustify prebuild of libgit2, instrumenting Rust to match.
#
#   crustify/scripts/cargo-variant.sh <variant> <cargo subcommand> [args...]
#
# <variant> is a `variants` key of crustify/artifacts/build.json: plain, coverage, asan-ubsan,
# tsan or bsan. Each variant uses its own target dir under target/.
# The safe crate's build script, in campaign mode, links the variant's static archive (its
# `static` in build.json) into each test binary, so the C runs under the instrumentation the
# Rust is built with here, one runtime serving both. Set CRUSTIFY_BUILD_DIR to a private build
# of the variant, which carries the same archive, to link it instead of the shared one.
set -euo pipefail
variant=${1:?usage: cargo-variant.sh <variant> <cargo subcommand> [args...]}
shift
here=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)
host=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
export CRUSTIFY_BUILD_VARIANT=$variant
export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=${CARGO_TARGET_DIR:-$here/target/$variant}
# pcre2-sys links the variant's side-campaign PCRE2, the one libgit2's C links, rather than
# building its vendored copy, which would shadow it in every test binary. The side campaigns'
# clones sit where the variant's build found their installs, beside the repository whose
# crustify/builds holds it (build.json's configure takes them from `$PWD/../../../..` in
# crustify/builds/<variant>): resolved physically through crustify/builds, which a worktree or
# a gate snapshot links to that repository's, so that every checkout finds the same ones.
side=$(realpath -m "$here/crustify/builds/$variant/../../../..")
export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="$side/pcre2-bindings/crustify/builds/$variant/install/lib/pkgconfig${PKG_CONFIG_PATH:+:$PKG_CONFIG_PATH}"
cd "$here"
# The nightly the workspace pins, for the sanitizers that need it.
nightly=$(sed -n 's/^nightly = "\(.*\)"$/\1/p' Cargo.toml)
# Cargo's own flags must come before a `--`, which hands the rest to the test binaries.
pre=() post=()
for arg in "$@"; do
  if [ ${#post[@]} -gt 0 ] || [ "$arg" = -- ]; then post+=("$arg"); else pre+=("$arg"); fi
done
case $variant in
  plain)
    exec cargo "$@" ;;
  coverage)
    # Source-based coverage on the pinned nightly, against the variant's clang-instrumented C,
    # which each test binary links statically, so that rustc's profiler runtime counts both;
    # crustify/scripts/coverage/ measures the suites as the testing spec's Coverage section does.
    export RUSTFLAGS="${RUSTFLAGS:-} -C instrument-coverage"
    export RUSTDOCFLAGS="${RUSTDOCFLAGS:-} -C instrument-coverage"
    export LLVM_PROFILE_FILE=${LLVM_PROFILE_FILE:-$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/profraw/%p-%m.profraw}
    exec cargo "+$nightly" "${pre[@]}" --target $host "${post[@]}" ;;
  asan-ubsan)
    export RUSTFLAGS="${RUSTFLAGS:-} -Zsanitizer=address -Cforce-frame-pointers=yes"
    export RUSTDOCFLAGS="${RUSTDOCFLAGS:-} -Zsanitizer=address"
    export ASAN_OPTIONS=${ASAN_OPTIONS:-detect_leaks=1:abort_on_error=1}
    export UBSAN_OPTIONS=${UBSAN_OPTIONS:-print_stacktrace=1:halt_on_error=1}
    exec cargo "+$nightly" "${pre[@]}" --target $host "${post[@]}" ;;
  tsan)
    export RUSTFLAGS="${RUSTFLAGS:-} -Zsanitizer=thread"
    export RUSTDOCFLAGS="${RUSTDOCFLAGS:-} -Zsanitizer=thread"
    # glibc's tzset locks what TSan cannot see: see tsan.supp.
    export TSAN_OPTIONS=${TSAN_OPTIONS:-halt_on_error=1:suppressions=$here/crustify/scripts/tsan.supp}
    exec cargo "+$nightly" "${pre[@]}" -Zbuild-std --target $host "${post[@]}" ;;
  bsan)
    # trybuild's nested cargo build does not finish under BorrowSanitizer, and the
    # compile-fail suite is a compile-time check the plain variant already runs.

# One feature per link unit; each gates its module in src/lib.rs, and src/sys.rs's when the
# link unit is optional.
libgit2 = []
# The CLI (src/cli), whose C links libgit2's: the bundled build compiles its objects, and
# the `shared` and `system` modes, whose libraries hold none, refuse it.
git2 = ["libgit2"]
# Regenerates the raw bindings into OUT_DIR from the headers of the C a build links, in
# place of the committed ones; campaign mode checks them against the committed ones
# (crustify's `bindgen` skill, Build modes).
bindgen = ["dep:bindgen"]
# Builds `c/` as shared libraries in place of static ones.
shared = []
# Links an install of libgit2, found through LIBGIT2_DIR or pkg-config, in place of `c/`.
system = []
# The export features: one per ported module not yet switched from C, which compiles its
# `ffi_export` gateway, the bare-named exports through which the remaining C calls it. Each
# stays off until its module switches, so that the exports never collide with the C they
# replace, and the switch deletes it (crustify's conventions, Export features). Those of
# `src/util/utf8.c`, `src/cli/opt.c`, `deps/llhttp/api.c` and `deps/llhttp/http.c` went at
# their switches.
# `src/util/hash/sha1dc/ubc_check.c`: `sha1_dvs` and `ubc_check`, for `sha1.c`.
ffi-export-src-util-hash-sha1dc-ubc-check-c = []

[dependencies]
# By path, not by Git: trybuild replaces only the paths of dependencies declared by path
# with `$FFIBOX` in compile-fail snapshots. By the canonical path of the campaign's own
# checkout of ffibox, the worktree of its working branch, `libgit2-crustify/devel`, so that
# the crate builds against the ffibox the campaign has changed, not against `devel`'s, which
# /crustify-rs/ffibox and the /opt/venv/share/ffibox link hold. Canonical, since trybuild
# replaces the canonicalized path while rustc prints the path as declared: a path through a
# link leaves the snapshots' paths absolute. glibc-bindings takes it by Git, which the [patch] below points at this path,
# so the graph holds one ffibox.
ffibox = { version = "0.1.1", path = "/crustify-rs/ffibox.libgit2-crustify" }
# libc's wrapper, the crustify-rs/glibc-crustify side campaign: pinned to a commit
# (`wrapper.pin` in crustify/artifacts/dependencies.json), and patched below to its clone
# beside this repository while the campaign extends it, by absolute path, which the batch
# worktrees under crustify/.worktrees resolve too.
glibc-bindings = { version = "0.1.0", git = "https://github.com/crustify-rs/glibc-crustify", rev = "24da93fc31a1788e73443cf4333d5037435d2d3f" }
pcre2-sys = "0.2"
nix = { version = "0.31.3", features = ["fs", "socket", "net", "poll", "process", "user", "feature", "signal", "mman", "time", "uio", "dir", "hostname"] }
flate2 = "1.1.11"

### `libgit2/src/util/hash/sha1dc/ubc_check.c` wave 221 batch 2: review of batch 0

Reviews `wave-221/batch-0` (`2492d2a9f`), the wrap of `st::dv_info_t` as `DvInfo`, for every
objective, to the depth of a wrapper its port replaces: its public API. One report,
`misc/dv-info-step-docs-omit-the-stored-states` (`nit`): `DvInfo`'s documentation gave every
step in `0..80` as one `sha1.c` saved a state for, where `sha1.c` saves only 58 and 65
(`ubc_check.h`'s `DOSTORESTATE58`/`DOSTORESTATE65`) and `sha1_recompression_step` aborts on any
other; the fix is documentation alone, and the API is unchanged. Test adequacy: an equality that
left out the type, the step or the bit passed `copies_and_equality_cover_every_field` (checked
by that mutant on `plain`); the test now compares records that differ in each field alone, and
fails on it. No new test, so the counts stand. The two `provisional` lessons,
`cmake-property-naming-a-removed-source` and `http-exports-gated-through-a-local-remote`, read
against `c/deps/llhttp/CMakeLists.txt` and `crustify/scripts/http-gate.sh`, are `held`. Gates:
`fmt --check` and `clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` on `plain`; the module's
`unit_pub` and `ub_safe` tests plain, under ASan+UBSan, TSan and Miri; the compile-fail suite
plain. No BSan run: the change reaches no reborrow. Coverage, one `run.sh` over the tree, read
with `report.py` from the scratch tree's `src/libgit2` (`C=@c` over `libcrustify.a`, Rust over the
scratch `src/`), the unit column merging `lib` and `unit_pub`; the pp cells are against batch 0's
measurement of the same base, and the C shifts are run-to-run variation, as no test reaching C
changed. ffimap (the batch-0 flags) moves only `code.tests.loc.total` (`+11`), the Overview's test
LoC; `ffimap api` against the base (nightly `2026-10-08`, ffibox's private rustdoc JSON): the 5
items `kept`, every unattributed module `kept`. Usage cells are the assistant's.

### `libgit2/src/util/hash/sha1dc/ubc_check.c` wave 221 batch 1: the module's `port`

The module's symbols, waves 221 and 222 folded into one batch on wave 221's branch, since
wave 222's two items use wave 221's: `mac::DVMASKSIZE`, the 32 `glb::DV_*_bit` constants
(16 of type I, 16 of type II; the task message's "33" counts one too many, `task.json` lists
32), `glb::sha1_dvs` and `fn::ubc_check`, in `src/libgit2/src/util/hash/sha1dc/ubc_check.rs`
beside batch 0's `DvInfo`. `DVMASKSIZE` is a `pub const usize` (1), each bit a `pub const u32`
(`DV_I_43_0_BIT` … `DV_II_56_0_BIT`), the table `SHA1_DVS: [DvInfo; 33]`, a `static` built at
compile time by a private `const fn dv` over `DvInfo::new`, which fails the build on a record
`sha1.c` could not read, and `ubc_check(&[u32; 80]) -> [u32; DVMASKSIZE]`, the out-parameter
returned. `ubc_check` is a statement-for-statement translation of the generated C, made by a
scratch translator from its expressions, with the C's wrapping 32-bit arithmetic
(`wrapping_sub`, `wrapping_neg`) and its guards kept, since a guarded condition whose value
is not all ones outside the guarded bits would clear others unguarded. Analysis: `W` is read
during the call only, words 35 to 64, and never kept; `dvmask` is written once; nothing fails
and no state is kept; `sha1_process` passes `ctx->m1`, which `sha1_compression_states` has
written whole, and its local `ubc_dv_mask`. `sha1_dvs` is read by `sha1_process` alone and
written by no C, so the table is immutable, in read-only memory. No out-of-tree entity is
used. The findings are submitted to the ownership store (`ubc_check`'s `lifetime: null`,
`sha1_dvs`'s `ptr` and `locked_by` null); the two parameters' pointer findings were refused,
wavefront listing no pointer parameter declared as an array
(`crustify/evolution/wavefront-array-parameters-are-pointers`).

content.content:
much of their building and testing overlaps, the memory and disk each one's tree takes, and
the rate the provider allows.

The number of agents in flight follows from those, for each wave as it starts and again as
its batches land or fail. A `parallelism` number in the settings' `workload` answer, or an
audit's `parallelism` answer, is a cap on it; the default, `assistant's choice`, sets none. When the waves of several modules, campaigns,
or of a campaign and its side campaigns, run at once, they share the host as one workload.

One unit of work may be given priority over another by suspending the other's agents, with
every process of their trees, and resuming them once the first has finished. A suspended
agent keeps its state; its interval then includes the suspension, and its record says so.

## 3. Jobs

Each build, test run and gate takes its parallelism when it starts, from the jobs already
running on the host: the job count of a build, the threads of a test binary, and the
number of gate invocations run side by side, such as Miri's or BSan's one per test binary.
The jobs of every workload on the host add up to about its core count: a workload that
runs alone takes the whole host, and one among many takes its share.

The jobs actually running are the measure, not the load average alone, which lags them and
counts what waits on I/O. Memory bounds a job count as well as cores do: a link or a
sanitized test binary can need more memory than a core's share.

The parallelism is given to each command through its environment, so that no command
carries it: `MAKEFLAGS=-j<n>` for Make, `CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL=<n>` for CMake,
`CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=<n>` for Cargo, and `RUST_TEST_THREADS=<n>` for Rust tests, or the build
system's own equivalent.

## 4. Artifacts

`crustify/artifacts/build.json`'s commands carry no job count. A job count does not change

every process of their trees, and resuming them once the first has finished. A suspended
agent keeps its state; its interval then includes the suspension, and its record says so.

## 3. Jobs

Each build, test run and gate takes its parallelism when it starts, from the jobs already
running on the host: the job count of a build, the threads of a test binary, and the
number of gate invocations run side by side, such as Miri's or BSan's one per test binary.
The jobs of every workload on the host add up to about its core count: a workload that
runs alone takes the whole host, and one among many takes its share.

The jobs actually running are the measure, not the load average alone, which lags them and
counts what waits on I/O. Memory bounds a job count as well as cores do: a link or a
sanitized test binary can need more memory than a core's share.

The parallelism is given to each command through its environment, so that no command
carries it: `MAKEFLAGS=-j<n>` for Make, `CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL=<n>` for CMake,
`CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=<n>` for Cargo, and `RUST_TEST_THREADS=<n>` for Rust tests, or the build
system's own equivalent.

change the variant, and does not raise the file's `version`. The `workload` answer's

    def lint(self) -> None:
        """The format check and the lints, on the snapshot's committed tree, once with no
        feature and once per `--lint-features`."""
        env = self.env("lint")
        self.run("lint", "lint-fmt", ["cargo", f"+{self.a.nightly}", "fmt", "--all", "--check"],
                 env)
        for features in ["", *self.a.lint_features]:
            name = "lint-clippy" + (f"-{features.replace(',', '+')}" if features else "")
            cmd = [*self.cargo("lint"), "clippy", "--workspace", "--all-targets"]
            if features:
                cmd += ["--features", features]
            self.run("lint", name, [*cmd, "--", "-D", "warnings"], env)

    def per_binary(self, stage: str, package: str, bins: list[str], skips) -> None:
        env = self.env(stage)
        build = self.run(stage, f"{stage}-build",
                         [*self.cargo(stage), "test", "-p", package, "--no-run"], env)
        if build["exit"] != 0:
            return
        timeout = self.a.timeout if stage == "bsan" else None

        def one(binary: str) -> None:
            names = list(skips.get(stage, {}).get(binary, []))
            if stage == "miri" and names:
                # `--exact` would make `compile_fail` exact too: name its tests.
                names += sorted(t for t in self.lists[stage, binary]
                                if "compile_fail" in t and t not in names)

        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=self.a.parallel or len(bins)) as pool:

# Where an exported global's storage is defined while its export feature is off

Status: `open`.

## Signal

A rule an agent had to work out by hand that a skill should state. `porting-symbols`'
Globals section has a ported global's storage held by Rust "from its port, beside its
module's C, which keeps its own copy until the switch; from then on the Rust's is the only
one", and a global the remaining C accesses "is exported, as a function is". The
conventions' Exports and Export features sections put every export in the module's
`ffi_export` gateway, compiled only under the export feature, which stays off until the
switch, and put every `#[unsafe(…)]` attribute in a region. For a function, the native
function and its export are two items, so the native one compiles with the feature off and
the export calls it. A global's export is its storage: the symbol C reads is the static
itself. With the feature off, the native API needs the storage, which the gateway cannot
hold; with it on, a second static in the gateway would make two Rust copies, against "the
Rust's is the only one"; and `#[unsafe(no_mangle)]` or `#[unsafe(export_name)]` on the
native static, under a `cfg_attr`, would put unsafe code outside the regions. No skill says
which of these a port takes, and the crate held no exported global to follow: the
switched modules' exports are all functions.

## Evidence

`wave-221/batch-1/run-1` (`src/util/hash/sha1dc/ubc_check.c`), whose table `sha1_dvs`
`sha1.c`'s C reads (`sha1_process`) and keeps reading through the export once the module
switches, since `sha1.c` stays C past the campaign's first ship point. The batch defined
the table's data once, as a private `const DVS`, and its storage under the two exclusive
configurations:

```rust
#[cfg(not(feature = "ffi-export-src-util-hash-sha1dc-ubc-check-c"))]
pub static SHA1_DVS: [DvInfo; DV_COUNT] = DVS;

#[cfg(feature = "ffi-export-src-util-hash-sha1dc-ubc-check-c")]
pub use self::ffi_export::sha1_dvs as SHA1_DVS;

// in `mod ffi_export`:
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub static sha1_dvs: [DvInfo; DV_COUNT] = DVS;
```

so that each build holds one Rust copy, which the native API names by its Rust name in
both, and the remaining C reads that copy once the feature is on. With the feature on, the
test binaries link it in place of the archive's `ubc_check.c.o`: `nm` shows one `sha1_dvs`,
`R`, and none of the TU's `static const` bit constants, and a gateway `unit_priv` test
checks that `&raw const sha1_dvs` and `&raw const SHA1_DVS` are one address.
`non_upper_case_globals`, which the workspace denies, exempts a `#[no_mangle]` static, and
`build.rs`'s `exported_name` reads the `pub static sha1_dvs` line as an export. At the
switch, deleting the feature removes the `cfg(not(…))` static and the `cfg` of the
re-export, and the storage stays the gateway's until the global's `port/unexport` moves it
back to the native code.

## Goal

Consistency (the same case written the same way in every module) and Interoperability
(one copy of each global, which the remaining C and the Rust share). Fitness: a review
finding of an exported global held twice, or of its export outside the gateway, which this
rule prevents.

## Destination

The spec: `porting-symbols`' Globals section, which the translator's role evolves; the
conventions' Exports section names it.

## Change

Not made yet, pending review of the pattern on this batch's module pass. One paragraph in
`porting-symbols`' Globals section, after "is exported, as a function is": the global's
data is one constant; while its export feature is off, the native static holds it under
`cfg(not(feature))`; under the feature, the gateway's `#[unsafe(no_mangle)]` static, under
the C name, is the storage, and the module re-exports it under the native name, so that
each build has one copy and the API's path does not change; the switch removes the native
static and the re-export's `cfg`; its `port/unexport` moves the storage back to the native
code. And a sentence in `porting-workflow`'s Builds section's first step, naming the
re-export among the mentions of the feature the switch rewrites.

## Record

The row for `EVOLUTION.md`, copied in when the change lands.

| change | from | landed as | signal answered | recurrence signal | status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| an exported global's one storage is the native static while its export feature is off and the gateway's `no_mangle` static, re-exported under the native name, once it is on | `libgit2-crustify`, `exported-global-storage-before-the-switch` | — | the first exported global of a port campaign had to work out where its storage is defined while its gateway compiles only under the export feature | an exported global held in two Rust copies, or exported from outside its gateway | watched |

## Validation

The batch above: `clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` with the feature off and on;
the module's tests plain, under ASan+UBSan, TSan and Miri with the feature off, and its
gateway's tests with it on, under Miri too; with the feature on, `sha1.c`'s own C
(`SHA1DCInit`, `SHA1DCUpdate`, `SHA1DCFinal`, called from a scratch test) still detects the
collision of `shattered-1.pdf` through the exported table and check, and does not once one
bit of the file changes.

## Review

#!/bin/bash
# Build the safe crate's Rust static library for a variant's own C to link (crustify's
# porting-workflow skill, Builds): once a module has switched from C, the remaining C, its
# library, CLI and tests, reaches the module through the crate's exports, and its CMake
# build links this library (`LIBGIT2_RUST_LIBRARY`).
#
#   rust-staticlib.sh <variant> <archive>
#
# Run from the variant's build dir, configured and not yet built, as the first step of its
# `build` command in crustify/artifacts/build.json; <archive> is the library written,
# relative to the build dir, as its configure's `-DLIBGIT2_RUST_LIBRARY` names it. The crate
# is the one of the checkout this script belongs to, built as a `staticlib` on the dev
# profile, the campaign's tests' own, in campaign mode against this build dir
# (`CRUSTIFY_BUILD_DIR`) with `CRUSTIFY_STATICLIB` set, so that it reads the build's headers
# and configuration and links none of its C, and with the `bindgen` feature, so that the
# committed bindings are checked against them. Its Rust is instrumented as
# crustify/scripts/cargo-variant.sh instruments <variant>'s, so that one runtime serves the C
# and the Rust of every C consumer. Cargo's target dir is the build's own, `crustify/cargo`;
# the archive is replaced atomically, so that a link never reads a partial one.
set -euo pipefail
usage='usage: rust-staticlib.sh <variant> <archive>'
variant=${1:?$usage}
archive=${2:?$usage}
[ $# -eq 2 ] || { echo "$usage" >&2; exit 2; }
here=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)
host=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
[ -f CMakeCache.txt ] && [ -f build.ninja ] || {
  echo "rust-staticlib.sh: $PWD is not a configured CMake build with the Ninja generator" >&2
  exit 2
}
build=$(pwd -P)
case $archive in /*) ;; *) archive=$build/$archive ;; esac

export CRUSTIFY_BUILD_DIR=$build CRUSTIFY_STATICLIB=1
export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$build/crustify/cargo
crate=(-p libgit2-crustify --lib --locked --features bindgen)
bundled=
case $variant in
  plain)
    out=$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/debug
    "$here/crustify/scripts/cargo-variant.sh" "$variant" rustc "${crate[@]}" --crate-type staticlib ;;
  coverage|asan-ubsan|tsan)
    out=$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/$host/debug
    "$here/crustify/scripts/cargo-variant.sh" "$variant" rustc "${crate[@]}" --crate-type staticlib ;;
  bsan)
    # `cargo bsan` drives `build`, `run` and `test` only, and a `build` cannot change a
    # crate's type. It sets its rustc driver up and runs the cargo CARGO names, so a stand-in
    # for that cargo turns its `build` into `rustc --crate-type staticlib`, every other call,
    # its `metadata` among them, passing through. The /opt shim of `cargo bsan` sets CARGO
    # itself, so the real cargo-bsan, the ELF on PATH, is run directly, as the shim runs it.
    out=$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/bsan/$host/debug
    real_cargo=$(type -P cargo)
    real_bsan=
    for c in $(type -ap cargo-bsan); do
      [ "$(head -c4 "$c")" = $'\x7fELF' ] && { real_bsan=$c; break; }
    done
    [ -n "$real_bsan" ] || { echo "rust-staticlib.sh: no cargo-bsan executable on PATH" >&2; exit 1; }
    mkdir -p "$CARGO_TARGET_DIR"
    shim=$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/cargo-rustc-staticlib
    printf '%s\n' '#!/bin/bash' \
      "[ \"\${1:-}\" = build ] || exec '$real_cargo' \"\$@\"" \
      'shift' \
      "exec '$real_cargo' rustc \"\$@\" --crate-type staticlib" >"$shim"
    chmod +x "$shim"
    side=$(realpath -m "$build/../../../..")
    export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="$side/pcre2-bindings/crustify/builds/$variant/install/lib/pkgconfig${PKG_CONFIG_PATH:+:$PKG_CONFIG_PATH}"
    export CRUSTIFY_BUILD_VARIANT=$variant
    (cd "$here" && RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=bsan CARGO=$shim "$real_bsan" bsan build "${crate[@]}")
    # The driver bundles BorrowSanitizer's C runtime into the library; the C's own links
    # link it (the variant's CMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS), so that each process holds it once,
    # and a shared library none: its members are removed from the copy written.
    bundled=$(rustc +bsan --print sysroot)/lib/libclang_rt.bsan-x86_64.a
    [ -f "$bundled" ] || { echo "rust-staticlib.sh: no BorrowSanitizer runtime at $bundled" >&2; exit 1; } ;;
  *)
    echo "rust-staticlib.sh: unknown variant: $variant" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

lib=$out/liblibgit2_crustify.a
[ -f "$lib" ] || { echo "rust-staticlib.sh: cargo wrote no $lib" >&2; exit 1; }
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$archive")"
tmp=$archive.tmp.$$
trap 'rm -f "$tmp"' EXIT
cp "$lib" "$tmp"
if [ -n "$bundled" ]; then
  mapfile -t members < <(ar t "$bundled" | sort -u)
  while ar t "$tmp" | grep -qxF -f <(printf '%s\n' "${members[@]}"); do

#!/bin/bash
# Build the safe crate's Rust static library for a variant's own C to link (crustify's
# porting-workflow skill, Builds): once a module has switched from C, the remaining C, its
# library, CLI and tests, reaches the module through the crate's exports, and its CMake
# build links this library (`LIBGIT2_RUST_LIBRARY`).
#
#   rust-staticlib.sh <variant> <archive>
#
# Run from the variant's build dir, configured and not yet built, as the first step of its
# `build` command in crustify/artifacts/build.json; <archive> is the library written,
# relative to the build dir, as its configure's `-DLIBGIT2_RUST_LIBRARY` names it. The crate
# is the one of the checkout this script belongs to, built as a `staticlib` on the dev
# profile, the campaign's tests' own, in campaign mode against this build dir
# (`CRUSTIFY_BUILD_DIR`) with `CRUSTIFY_STATICLIB` set, so that it reads the build's headers
# and configuration and links none of its C, and with the `bindgen` feature, so that the
# committed bindings are checked against them. Its Rust is instrumented as
# crustify/scripts/cargo-variant.sh instruments <variant>'s, so that one runtime serves the C
# and the Rust of every C consumer. Cargo's target dir is the build's own, `crustify/cargo`;
# the archive is replaced atomically, so that a link never reads a partial one.
set -euo pipefail
usage='usage: rust-staticlib.sh <variant> <archive>'
variant=${1:?$usage}
archive=${2:?$usage}
[ $# -eq 2 ] || { echo "$usage" >&2; exit 2; }
here=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)
host=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
[ -f CMakeCache.txt ] && [ -f build.ninja ] || {
  echo "rust-staticlib.sh: $PWD is not a configured CMake build with the Ninja generator" >&2
  exit 2
}
build=$(pwd -P)
case $archive in /*) ;; *) archive=$build/$archive ;; esac

export CRUSTIFY_BUILD_DIR=$build CRUSTIFY_STATICLIB=1
export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$build/crustify/cargo
crate=(-p libgit2-crustify --lib --locked --features bindgen)
bundled=
case $variant in
  plain)
    out=$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/debug
    "$here/crustify/scripts/cargo-variant.sh" "$variant" rustc "${crate[@]}" --crate-type staticlib ;;
  coverage|asan-ubsan|tsan)
    out=$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/$host/debug
    "$here/crustify/scripts/cargo-variant.sh" "$variant" rustc "${crate[@]}" --crate-type staticlib ;;
  bsan)
    # `cargo bsan` drives `build`, `run` and `test` only, and a `build` cannot change a
    # crate's type. It sets its rustc driver up and runs the cargo CARGO names, so a stand-in
    # for that cargo turns its `build` into `rustc --crate-type staticlib`, every other call,
    # its `metadata` among them, passing through. The /opt shim of `cargo bsan` sets CARGO
    # itself, so the real cargo-bsan, the ELF on PATH, is run directly, as the shim runs it.
    out=$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/bsan/$host/debug
    real_cargo=$(type -P cargo)
    real_bsan=
    for c in $(type -ap cargo-bsan); do
      [ "$(head -c4 "$c")" = $'\x7fELF' ] && { real_bsan=$c; break; }
    done
    [ -n "$real_bsan" ] || { echo "rust-staticlib.sh: no cargo-bsan executable on PATH" >&2; exit 1; }
    mkdir -p "$CARGO_TARGET_DIR"
    shim=$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/cargo-rustc-staticlib
    printf '%s\n' '#!/bin/bash' \
      "[ \"\${1:-}\" = build ] || exec '$real_cargo' \"\$@\"" \
      'shift' \
      "exec '$real_cargo' rustc \"\$@\" --crate-type staticlib" >"$shim"
    chmod +x "$shim"
    side=$(realpath -m "$build/../../../..")
    export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="$side/pcre2-bindings/crustify/builds/$variant/install/lib/pkgconfig${PKG_CONFIG_PATH:+:$PKG_CONFIG_PATH}"
    export CRUSTIFY_BUILD_VARIANT=$variant
    (cd "$here" && RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=bsan CARGO=$shim "$real_bsan" bsan build "${crate[@]}")

    # link it (the variant's CMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS), so that each process holds it once,
    # and a shared library none: its members are removed from the copy written.
    bundled=$(rustc +bsan --print sysroot)/lib/libclang_rt.bsan-x86_64.a
    [ -f "$bundled" ] || { echo "rust-staticlib.sh: no BorrowSanitizer runtime at $bundled" >&2; exit 1; } ;;
  *)
    echo "rust-staticlib.sh: unknown variant: $variant" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

lib=$out/liblibgit2_crustify.a

tmp=$archive.tmp.$$
trap 'rm -f "$tmp"' EXIT
cp "$lib" "$tmp"

fi

rm -rf "$out/ctest"
mkdir -p "$out/ctest"
(cd "$d" && find . -name CTestTestfile.cmake -not -path './crustify/*' -exec cp --parents {} "$out/ctest" \;)
# It runs beside the suites below, as one more job.
(
  ctest --test-dir "$out/ctest" --output-on-failure -R '^(offline|util)$' >"$out/ctest.log" 2>&1
  echo $? >"$out/ctest.rc"
) &
ctest_pid=$!

# 2. Every suite alone.
rm -rf "$out/suites"
for b in libgit2_tests util_tests; do
  mkdir -p "$out/suites/$b"
  "$d/$b" -l 2>/dev/null | sed -nE 's/^ *[0-9]+: (.*)$/\1/p' | grep -v '^online::' |
    D="$d" O="$out" B="$b" xargs -P "$jobs" -I{} bash -c \
      'cd "$O" && timeout 1800 "$D/$B" -t "-s$1" > "suites/$B/$1.tap" 2> "suites/$B/$1.err"; echo $? > "suites/$B/$1.rc"' _ {}
done

wait "$ctest_pid"

# 3. The tally, against the baseline.
python3 -I "$here/c-tests-tally.py" "$out" "$here/../artifacts/c-baseline.json" "$variant"
status=$?
echo "c-tests.sh: ctest exited $(cat "$out/ctest.rc") ($out/ctest.log)"
exit $status

#!/bin/bash
# Archive the objects every link unit links into one static archive, so that campaign mode
# links the C statically and reaches the internal functions the shared library hides
# (crustify's setup skill, Builds; bindgen, Build modes).
#
#   static-archive.sh <archive> <link unit>...
#
# Run from a variant's build dir, as the last step of its `build` command, once the build is
# current: <archive> is the archive written, relative to the build dir, as the variant's
# `static` records it in crustify/artifacts/build.json, and each <link unit> names a target
# CMake links: a shared library by its name (libgit2, for libgit2.so) or an executable (git2,
# the CLI). The objects are taken from the build system, the explicit inputs of the edge that
# links each, found through its symlink edges: every TU of the link unit itself and of the
# object libraries it bundles, and nothing else (no test or other target). An object two
# link units both link (the CLI links libgit2's) is archived once, where it first appears.
# Nothing is compiled; the archive is replaced atomically and is deterministic (no
# timestamps), so the same objects give the same bytes.
set -euo pipefail
usage='usage: static-archive.sh <archive> <link unit>...'
archive=${1:?$usage}
shift
[ $# -gt 0 ] || { echo "$usage" >&2; exit 2; }
[ -f build.ninja ] || { echo "static-archive.sh: no build.ninja in $PWD" >&2; exit 2; }

# `ninja -t query` prints a target's rule on its `input:` line, then its explicit inputs
# indented by four spaces, its implicit ones after `| ` and its order-only ones after `|| `.
objects=() names=()
declare -A seen=()
for unit in "$@"; do
  target=$unit.so

input.command:
cat > sweep.py <<'EOF'
import re, subprocess, concurrent.futures as cf, sys, os
h = open('harness.rs').read(); f = open('fn.rs').read()
orig = f.replace('pub fn ubc_check', 'fn orig')
eq = '''
fn differs() -> bool {
    for (seed, _) in WITNESSES { let w = seeded(seed);
        for word in 0..80 { for flip in 0..32 { let mut c = w; c[word] ^= 1 << flip; if ubc_check(&c) != orig(&c) { return true; } } } }
    for seed in 0..(1u64 << 17) { let w = seeded(seed); if ubc_check(&w) != orig(&w) { return true; } }
    false
}
'''
h = h.replace('fn main() { println!("{} {}", old() as u8, new() as u8); }',
              'fn main() { println!("{} {} {}", old() as u8, new() as u8, differs() as u8); }')
muts = []
for m in re.finditer(r'w\[(\d+)\]', f):
    n = int(m.group(1)); k = n + 1 if n < 79 else n - 1
    muts.append((f'w[{n}]->w[{k}] at {f[:m.start()].count(chr(10))+1}', f[:m.start()] + f'w[{k}]' + f[m.end():]))
for m in re.finditer(r'\(1 << (\d+)\)', f):
    n = int(m.group(1)); k = (n + 1) % 32
    muts.append((f'1<<{n}->1<<{k} at {f[:m.start()].count(chr(10))+1}', f[:m.start()] + f'(1 << {k})' + f[m.end():]))
for m in re.finditer(r'(?<![=!])(==|!=) 0', f):
    k = '!=' if m.group(1) == '==' else '=='
    muts.append((f'{m.group(1)}->{k} at {f[:m.start()].count(chr(10))+1}', f[:m.start()] + f'{k} 0' + f[m.end():]))
os.makedirs('sweep', exist_ok=True)
def run(i):
    name, body = muts[i]
    src = f'sweep/m{i}.rs'; exe = f'sweep/m{i}'
    open(src, 'w').write(h.replace('/*FN*/', body + orig + eq))
    c = subprocess.run(['rustc', '--edition', '2024', '-C', 'opt-level=1', '-A', 'warnings', '-o', exe, src], capture_output=True, text=True)
    if c.returncode: return name, 'build-fail'
    r = subprocess.run([exe], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=600).stdout.split()
    os.remove(exe); os.remove(src)
    return name, ' '.join(r)
with cf.ThreadPoolExecutor(12) as ex:
    res = list(ex.map(run, range(len(muts))))
for name, r in res: print(name, r)
EOF

class: nit
evidence: the C contradicts the documentation (`c/src/util/hash/sha1dc/ubc_check.h:39-40`, `c/src/util/hash/sha1dc/sha1.c:1301-1707,1743`)
conditions: any; `src/libgit2/src/util/hash/sha1dc/ubc_check.rs` at `2492d2a9f`, the C at the fork's `230c9dbdb`

# `DvInfo`'s step documents every step in `0..80` as one `sha1.c` saved a state for

**Where.** `src/libgit2/src/util/hash/sha1dc/ubc_check.rs` on `2492d2a9f`:
`DvInfoRef::recompression_step`'s first sentence, "The step `sha1.c` recompresses from, in
`0..80`: the index of the state it saved at that step", and `DvInfo::new`, whose only word on
the step is that one outside `0..80` is refused "where `sha1.c` could not read the record".

**What is wrong.** `sha1.c` saves the state of a step only where `DOSTORESTATE<step>` is
defined, and `ubc_check.h`, this module's header, defines two: `DOSTORESTATE58` and
`DOSTORESTATE65`. `sha1_recompression_step` has a `case` only for those steps and
`default: abort();`, and `sha1_process` calls it with `sha1_dvs[i].testt` (`sha1.c:1743`). So
`new` accepts a step, such as 10, that `sha1.c` would read without going out of bounds but
then abort on, and the getter's text says a state was saved at it. The bound `new` keeps is
the one memory safety needs, the index into `ctx->states[80]`, and is right; what the
documentation leaves out is the narrower set of steps the C recompresses from, which the
batch's own analysis records (`crustify/wavefront/ownership-store.json`, `dv_info_t`'s
`_comment_user`: "`sha1_recompression_step` aborts on a step without `DOSTORESTATE`, 58 and 65
here") but which reached no reader of the API. `sha1.c`'s port, which keeps this type's API,
reads it from there.

Nothing a consumer can observe: no safe API hands a `DvInfo` to C, which reads only
`sha1_dvs`, and every record of the C table has step 58 or 65 (32 records and the terminator,
whose type ends the scan before its step is read). Hence `nit`, with no reproducer.

**Check.**

```
grep -n 'DOSTORESTATE' c/src/util/hash/sha1dc/ubc_check.h          # 39, 40: 58 and 65
sed -n 1700,1707p c/src/util/hash/sha1dc/sha1.c                     # default: abort();
grep -n 'sha1_recompression_step(sha1_dvs' c/src/util/hash/sha1dc/sha1.c   # 1743
```

**Fix.** `DvInfo::new`'s documentation adds that not every step in range is one `sha1.c`
recompresses from, names the two `ubc_check.h` saves, and says `sha1_recompression_step`
aborts on any other and that a table `sha1.c` reads holds those alone; the getter says the
state is saved only for 58 and 65. `new` keeps accepting `0..80`: the narrower set is a
configuration of `sha1.c` (its `DOSTORESTATE` macros), which its port may change, and refusing
by it would tie the type's invariant to that configuration with no safety gain. The API is
unchanged.

**Tiers.** Caught by this review batch (`wave-221/batch-2`), the first tier after the batch
that wrote the type (`wave-221/batch-0`), whose own gates had it in scope.

input.content:
class: nit
evidence: the source (`src/libgit2/src/util/hash/sha1dc/ubc_check.rs:821-825` at `e816c88bb`), and rustdoc's search index of a crate that re-exports a static as this one does
conditions: the export feature `ffi-export-src-util-hash-sha1dc-ubc-check-c` on, as every build is once the module switches from C; `src/libgit2/src/util/hash/sha1dc/ubc_check.rs` at `e816c88bb`

# `SHA1_DVS` loses its `sha1_dvs` alias, and its description, once the export feature is on

**Where.** `src/libgit2/src/util/hash/sha1dc/ubc_check.rs` on `e816c88bb`. The table has two
definitions, one per state of the export feature:

```rust
/// The disturbance vectors SHA-1 collision detection checks, generated by `parse_bitrel` …
///
/// Replaces `glb::sha1_dvs`
#[doc(alias = "sha1_dvs")]
#[cfg(not(feature = "ffi-export-src-util-hash-sha1dc-ubc-check-c"))]
pub static SHA1_DVS: [DvInfo; DV_COUNT] = DVS;

#[cfg(feature = "ffi-export-src-util-hash-sha1dc-ubc-check-c")]
pub use self::ffi_export::sha1_dvs as SHA1_DVS;
```

**What is wrong.** The conventions' Anchors section gives the item that stands in for a C item
two attributes, the anchor and the alias, "so that a consumer who searches the documentation
for the source's name finds every item that stands in for it". With the feature off,
`SHA1_DVS` has both. With it on, `SHA1_DVS` is the re-export of the gateway's
`#[unsafe(no_mangle)] pub static sha1_dvs`, whose documentation carries the anchor but cannot
carry the alias, since rustdoc rejects an alias equal to its item's own name, and the re-export
carries neither an alias nor a word of documentation of its own. Rustdoc inlines the re-export
of an item of a private module under the re-export's name, `SHA1_DVS`, so a search for
`sha1_dvs` no longer finds it, and its page holds only the gateway's text, which describes the
storage `sha1.c` reads and not the table the native API offers.

The feature is off in every build until the module's switch, and the switch, which follows
this pass, deletes it together with the `cfg(not(…))` static: from then on the re-export is
the table's only definition, and the alias and the description would be gone from the crate's
documentation for good. Nothing a consumer's code can observe; hence `nit`, with no reproducer.

**Check.** A crate that re-exports a `no_mangle` static of a private module, with and without
`#[doc(alias = "sha1_dvs")]` on the `pub use`: the alias reaches the search index only with
it (`rustdoc 1.x`, `search.index/alias/*` holds the entry, and no index file names `sha1_dvs`
without it):

```
mkdir -p /tmp/alias && cd /tmp/alias
cat > lib.rs <<'EOF'
//! x
mod inner {
    /// The table.
    #[unsafe(no_mangle)]
    pub static sha1_dvs: [u32; 2] = [1, 2];
}
/// The re-export's own doc.
#[doc(alias = "sha1_dvs")]
pub use self::inner::sha1_dvs as SHA1_DVS;
EOF
sed '/doc(alias/d' lib.rs > lib2.rs
rustdoc --edition 2024 --crate-type lib lib.rs -o with
rustdoc --edition 2024 --crate-type lib --crate-name lib lib2.rs -o without
grep -rl sha1_dvs with/search.index | wc -l      # 1
grep -rl sha1_dvs without/search.index | wc -l   # 0
```

In the crate itself the index names `sha1_dvs` with the feature on at `e816c88bb` too, as the
raw binding `sys::libgit2::sha1_dvs`, which is not the item a consumer uses in place of the C
global.

**Fix.** The re-export takes `#[doc(alias = "sha1_dvs")]` and the first paragraph of the
native static's description, which rustdoc shows before the gateway's text, so that with the
feature on `SHA1_DVS` has the alias, the description and, from the gateway, the anchor once
each. At the switch, the `cfg(not(…))` static goes and the re-export keeps all three.

**Tiers.** Caught by this module pass (`wave-221/batch-3`), the first review tier of the
code: `wave-221/batch-1`'s own gates had it in scope, and lint with the feature on, which
does not check anchors.

---
name: accounting
description: "The dashboard, its cells, the runs' records and transcripts, and how cost and time are derived. Read before filling dashboard cells or collecting a run's records."
---

# Accounting

What a campaign records about its own work: the dashboard, the runs' records and
transcripts its figures come from, and how cost and time are derived from them.

## 1. The dashboard

The dashboard, `crustify/artifacts/dashboard.md` unless the settings name another, is the
campaign's record of what each planner run, batch, wave and module did and cost. It is
filled from `templates/translate/dashboard.template.md`, an audit's from
`templates/audit/dashboard.template.md`, and keeps the template's format exactly.
When an adopted Crustify change adds a table or a column to the template, it is
added to the dashboard on the working branch before the next batch launches: a batch
fills the rows of the tables in place, and never adds one.

It is tracked in the campaign's tree, so every agent's worktree holds a copy, and it is
filled as the work lands rather than at the end. Each figure is measured once, where it is
produced: no suite or scan is rerun only to record one.

## 2. Cells

The dashboard's cells fall into three kinds, by when their figures can be known.

### 2.1 Landing cells

The cells measured on the tree a landing commits:

- for a batch, under the route its items' `kind` selects, as
  [`task-schema`](../../artifacts/task-schema/SKILL.md)'s Routes section gives it: its rows
  in that route's `Batches`, tests, `Batches: safety audit` and `Batches: API stability` tables, and for a review batch in
  `Batches — review: PoC + reports`, each placed in module, wave and batch order under
  its `pass`, and for a module pass, which spans both routes, in `Module passes`; those
  tables' `Σ` rows; and the `Coverage stats` table and the Overview's LoC
  line;
- for a planner run, its row in `Planning`, but for its usage cells.

They are filled in the landing's last commit, and measured against the integration branch
tip it was rebased onto: coverage as [`testing-builds`](../../verification/testing/builds/SKILL.md)'s Coverage section measures
it, the safety audit columns as the changes in the dashboard's Safety audit metrics, and
the API stability columns as the changes to the API of the landing's items are classified. A
rebase that conflicts in the dashboard keeps every row both sides added, and the landing's
cells, `Σ` rows included, are measured again where the gates its rebase reruns cover them;
the others stand as measured on the batch's base.

An integration merge, and any merge of one branch into another, keeps every row both
sides added, and settles the rest so: an additive `Σ` cell is the sum over the merged
rows, ours plus theirs less the merge base's, and so are the Overview's `Rust LoC`
figures; a usage `Σ` cell, its per-unit cells included, sums only the rows that carry
usage, so that it is filled again with theirs; a coverage `Σ` cell, and the Overview's
`C LoC`, are the later landing's; and `Coverage stats` takes the merged suites' counts,
with the later landing's percentages until a gate measures the merged tree, which the
merge commit's message says. A table or section the template holds once is kept once,
with the rows of every copy, whether or not the merge conflicts there, and the merged
dashboard is checked for repeated headings before it is committed.

### 2.2 Usage cells

The cells known only once an agent has ended, from its usage: its cost, tokens and wall,
the per-unit costs derived from them, and their `Σ` cells. A batch's are filled on the
working branch once its row is there, once its module is integrated, as
[`versioning`](../versioning/SKILL.md) describes, or, for a port's later-stage batch, which
runs after its module's switch, once its wave is promoted. A planner run's are filled once the run is
promoted. A batch run more than once costs the sum of its runs.

### 2.3 Campaign cells

The cells that span agents: the `Module stats` table, the Overview's branch line and
test baseline, and the `Settings` lines. A module's row and the branch line are filled
when the module is integrated, and a port's module row again as each of its later-stage
waves is promoted, the baseline once it is recorded, and the `Settings` lines,
with a Notes entry, whenever a settings change is applied.

### 2.4 Side campaign cells

A side campaign keeps its own dashboard, in its own repository, and its figures are
measured there. The parent's `Side campaigns` table copies them, one row per wrapper, as
they stand at the commit the parent pins, and the `side campaigns` row of `Module stats`
sums the rows, so that the parent's `Σ campaign` covers what its side campaigns cost. A
wrapper's row is filled each time the parent's pin moves, and its `shipped at` cell when
the wrapper ships the commit the parent pins. A side campaign that serves several parents
appears in each, with the figures as of each one's pin.

An audit's dashboard follows the same kinds over its own tables.

## 3. Records

Every run's `task.json` records how its agent ran: its backend, billing, model proxy and
the arguments its CLI was given, and, once it starts, its `session_id`, which ties the run
to its session. The session's transcript, which its CLI keeps by session id, is the
agent's full log and the source of its accounting. An agent spawned as a subagent of
another session has no session of its own: its session id is `agent-<agent id>`, the
name its host gives its transcript, under the spawning session's `subagents/`.

A transcript is copied into crustify's home, as `transcripts/<session id>.jsonl`, as soon
as its agent ends, because the CLIs move and prune their own files. Its usage is derived
from the copy, as [`usage`](../usage/SKILL.md) describes, with the backend and model proxy its
`task.json` names.

An evolution review is a run like any other: its `task.json` sits in its artifact dir, and
its transcript is collected and priced the same way, its cost counted with the sessions that
orchestrate the campaign and recorded, with its tokens and wall time, in its proposal's
Review section, so that what each review bought can be weighed against its cost.

The sessions that orchestrate the campaign are collected the same way: at the start of each session, the
transcripts of the sessions before it. A resumed session keeps its id while its transcript
grows: its transcript is copied again after each run, replacing the earlier copy. The
records, transcripts and rates stay in crustify's home.

## 4. Cost and time

A run's cost and tokens are its usage's `total.cost_usd` and `total.tokens`, as
[`usage`](../usage/SKILL.md) derives them from its transcript. The computed cost is used, never a provider-reported
dollar total; under subscription billing it is the API-equivalent cost.

An agent's wall time is its usage's interval. A wave's runs from its first batch's
launch through its final review and regression gates, a review wave's in an audit through
its landing, and a module's from its first launch through its final gate.

---
name: ffimap
description: "Deterministic counts and sites of a Rust crate's unsafe and FFI surface. Read before a batch lands (its safe-boundary scan and safety-audit cells), when reviewing for unsafety, contracts or UB, and, as a hint only, when planning an audit's scope and worksets."
---

# ffimap

ffimap maps a Rust crate's FFI and unsafe surface deterministically: a rustc driver over
HIR and typeck counts unsafe blocks and fns, raw and void pointers by position and
visibility, FFI calls and wrapper use. No model is involved, so two runs over one tree
agree exactly. Its `--help` lists its flags, and its `docs/schema.md`, read in full before
its first scan, its counters and how a report combines them.

It counts what the build compiles of the safe crate itself, and prints one JSON document:

```bash
ffimap <workdir> > <file>.json
```

Every scan names the crate's seams, the functions that hand a value between its wrapper and
its raw form, so that each counter's `of_which.seam` share tells that plumbing apart from
the pointer management a consumer of the safe API faces: ffibox's handle seams `as_ptr`,
`as_mut_ptr`, `as_void_ptr`, `from_ptr` and `from_void_ptr`, the ownership hand-offs
`from_raw_parts`, `into_raw_parts`, `into_raw`, `from_c`, `into_c` and `as_c_ptr`, the adoption of a raw C
value, `from_raw`, and the view of a C object as another, `as_object`. A crate built on
ffibox is scanned with `--ffibox`, and its `-sys` crates are named with `--sys-crates`:

```bash
ffimap <workdir> --ffibox --sys-crates <the -sys crates> --regions ffi_import,ffi_export \
    --seams as_ptr,as_mut_ptr,as_void_ptr,from_ptr,from_void_ptr,from_raw_parts,into_raw_parts,into_raw,from_c,into_c,as_c_ptr,from_raw,as_object \
    > <file>.json
```

Raw bindings that are a module of the crate, not a crate of their own, laid out and
generated as [`bindgen`](../../rust/bindgen/SKILL.md) describes, are named to `--sys-crates`

how a report is built from them. Every counter is determined from declarations
and single expression nodes -- no value is followed, no cast chain is composed,
and no dataflow is performed.

What each counter is decided FROM, and how a scan runs, is
[`analysis.md`](analysis.md); the ffibox vocabulary the `<trait>` and
`<primitive>` arms are generated from is [`ffibox.md`](ffibox.md).

## 1. The counters

Each row below is one counter, named by its dotted path into the document's
`counts`. A `{a,b}` is a split the counter carries: `raw_ptr.field.{pub,priv}`
is two leaves, and every row's leaves are integers. Each partition also carries
a `total`, derived from its children unless the driver emits it, so
`raw_ptr.field.total` exists and `raw_ptr.field.pub + raw_ptr.field.priv`
equals it; the `of_which` rows are shares of the row above them and are never
summed ([2.1](#21-partitions-and-shares)).

The counters are the whole of the document's `counts`. There is no second,
flat counter block beside them, and no prose rendering of them: a reader who
wants a rate divides the leaves it names.

Across the tree, `unsafe` and `safe` are the safety of the *function* the
position or site is in, `pub` and `priv` whether a consumer of the crate can
reach the item, and `void` a pointer whose pointee is erased (`*c_void`). A row
naming `ffibox`, a `<trait>` or a `<primitive>` is present only under
`--ffibox`, an `of_which.seam` row only with `--seams`, and a `region` or
`outside_regions` row only with `--regions`; each is absent rather than zero
otherwise ([2.3](#23-zero-and-absent)). A row ends with the property it bears
on, as [goals.md](goals.md) names them: safety, soundness, ergonomics or
idiomaticity.

### 1.1 `raw_ptr`

The raw pointers the crate declares in its signatures and types, and what its
bodies do with them.

- `raw_ptr.total.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- the denominator: every
  raw-pointer position the crate CHOSE, which is `fn_sig_arg` plus
  `fn_sig_ret` plus `field`. Emitted rather than derived, so it is not a sum of
  the families beside it ([analysis 9.2](analysis.md#92-what-raw_ptrtotal-admits)).
- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- raw pointers an argument of
  a signature takes. Taking is the hazard: a safe fn that takes one lets a
  caller pass anything with no `unsafe` at the call site.
- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg.of_which.void.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- of those, the
  erased ones. Subtract the share for the typed ones.
- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg.of_which.seam.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- of those, the
  ones in a function `--seams` declared to be nothing but a conversion between
  a wrapper and its raw pointer.
- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_ret.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- raw pointers a signature
  returns. Returning one still forces the caller to write `unsafe` before it
  means anything, which is why it is counted apart from `fn_sig_arg`.
- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_ret.of_which.void.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- as above.
- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_ret.of_which.seam.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- as above.
- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_trait_impl.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- positions in a trait
  impl's method, both directions in one counter: a trait declaration fixed the
  signature, so the crate did not choose the position, and the figure would
  otherwise move with how many types a trait is implemented for
  ([analysis 9.3](analysis.md#93-positions-a-trait-fixed)).
- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_trait_impl.of_which.void.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- as above.
- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_trait_impl.of_which.seam.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- as above.
- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_trait_impl.of_which.std.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- of
  those, the ones a standard-library trait fixed.
- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_trait_impl.of_which.local.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- the
  ones a trait the crate declared itself fixed.
- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_trait_impl.of_which.ffibox.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- the
  ones an ffibox contract fixed, which for a crate built on the convention is
  its lifecycle strategies.
- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_trait_impl.of_which.ffibox.of_which.<trait>` -- those by
  trait, over the whole vocabulary, so a document says which contracts reach a
  raw pointer and which do not. No safety or visibility split: a trait method's
  are the declaration's ([2.5](#25-deliberate-asymmetries)).
- `raw_ptr.field.{pub,priv}` -- struct and union fields declared with a raw
  pointer. `pub` is one reachability question, the type exported AND the field
  exported, rather than two levels a reader has to combine.
- `raw_ptr.field.of_which.void.{pub,priv}` -- of those, the erased ones.
- `raw_ptr.deref.{rd,wr}` -- dereference sites in bodies, by whether the place
  is read or written. Sites, not positions, so they are outside `raw_ptr.total`.
- `raw_ptr.casted_to.std.{owner,string,borrow,slice,other}` -- a raw pointer
  converted into a standard-library shape, by the shape it became: an owner
  (`Box`, `Vec`, `Rc`, `Arc`), a string (`CStr`, `CString`, `String`), a
  borrow, a slice. `other` is a shape the table does not know, which for `std`
  is none of them ([analysis 11.3](analysis.md#113-other)).
- `raw_ptr.casted_to.ffibox.{owner,string,borrow,slice}` -- adopted into an
  ffibox primitive, by the primitive's group. There is no `other` arm: every
  primitive maps to a shape.
- `raw_ptr.casted_to.local_seam.{owner,string,borrow,slice,other}` -- converted
  through a function `--seams` named, by the seam's return type. `other` is a
  seam returning a bespoke handle.
- `raw_ptr.surrendered.std.{owner,string}` -- the other direction: a value
  Rust owns turned into a raw pointer by a standard-library call, such as
  `Box::into_raw` or `CString::into_raw`, by the shape it had. What C is then
  trusted to give back to the allocator that made it (soundness).
- `raw_ptr.surrendered.ffibox.<shape>` -- the same through an ffibox
  primitive's `into_raw`, `into_c` or `into_raw_parts`, by the primitive's
  shape, as `casted_to.ffibox` reads it (soundness).

### 1.2 `ty`

The types the crate defines, by what they hold and what they declare about it.

- `ty.total.{pub,priv}` -- every type the crate defines. Emitted, and the
  denominator its shares are read against.
- `ty.total.of_which.std_trait.{pub,priv}` -- of those, the types that
  implement a standard-library trait.
- `ty.total.of_which.local_trait.{pub,priv}` -- the types that implement a
  trait the crate declared itself.
- `ty.total.of_which.ffibox_trait.{pub,priv}` -- the types that implement an
  ffibox contract.
- `ty.total.of_which.no_trait.{pub,priv}` -- the residual: types that
  implement no trait at all.
- `ty.total.of_which.macro.{pub,priv}` -- the types a macro wrote, such as
  `bitflags!`'s: subtract for the hand-written ones, as for `fn.total`.
- `ty.total.of_which.{repr_c,repr_transparent}.{pub,priv}` -- the types whose
  layout is C's (`#[repr(C)]`) or exactly another type's
  (`#[repr(transparent)]`): the layouts the crate shares with C (soundness).
- `ty.total.of_which.std_impl.<trait>.{pub,priv}` -- the types that implement
  one of a fixed list of std traits a Rust consumer expects of a value, by
  trait: `Debug`, `Display`, `Error`, `Clone`, `Default`, `PartialEq`, `Eq`,
  `Hash`, `Iterator` and `From`, derived or written (idiomaticity).
- `ty.storing_raw_ptr.{pub,priv}` -- types whose fields reach a raw pointer,
  within the peel set, so these are the types that manage one themselves
  rather than delegating to `Vec` or to an ffibox owner
  ([analysis 9.1](analysis.md#91-the-peel-set)).
- `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.impl_drop.{pub,priv}` -- of those, the ones that
  implement `Drop`: they free memory Rust did not allocate.
- `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.impl_clone.{pub,priv}` -- the ones that
  implement `Clone`, where a shallow clone duplicates the pointer and, with
  `Drop`, double-frees it.
- `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.{impl_deref,impl_deref_mut}.{pub,priv}` -- the
  ones that hand out a reference derived from the pointer implicitly, at every
  call site.
- `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.impl_send_sync.{pub,priv}` -- the ones that
  assert thread safety for memory no type system checked.
- `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.has_lifetime.{pub,priv}` -- the ones that tie
  the pointer to a lifetime parameter.
- `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.ffibox.{pub,priv}` -- the ones that declare
  their lifecycle through an ffibox contract, which none of the std shares can
  see.
- `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.pub_field.{pub,priv}` -- the ones that publish
  the pointer as a public field. Not a declaration: an access the type does not
  govern.
- `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.none.{pub,priv}` -- the residual: the type
  stores a pointer and declares nothing about it, in any vocabulary.
- `ty.wrapping_unsafe_cell.{pub,priv}` -- types holding an `UnsafeCell`, the
  one way to hold a value C may write while Rust holds a shared reference to it.
- `ty.impl_block.{pub,priv}` -- inherent `impl T` blocks: the API the crate
  wrote for its own type.
- `ty.impl_block.of_which.ffibox.{layout,ref,mut,locked}.{pub,priv}` -- of
  those, the blocks on a cell and on each of its handles, which are different
  surfaces: the layout type carries the constructors, the shared handle the
  getters, the exclusive handle the setters.
- `ty.impl_block.of_which.other.{pub,priv}` -- the blocks on everything else.
- `ty.impl_trait.{pub,priv}` -- `impl Tr for T` blocks: satisfying someone
  else's shape.
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.unsafe` -- of those, the `unsafe impl`s, which assert
  what the compiler cannot check. `TrivialClone`, which `#[derive(Clone)]`
  emits, is skipped.
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.derived.{pub,priv}` -- the ones a `#[derive]` wrote.
  Nobody typed them, and they are most of the `std` arm.
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.drop.{pub,priv}` -- the impls of a
  standard-library trait, by trait: `Drop`, which runs code when an object is
  released.
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.clone.{pub,priv}` -- `Clone`, which duplicates
  one.
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.send.{pub,priv}` -- `Send`, the claim that an
  object may move to another thread.
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.sync.{pub,priv}` -- `Sync`, the claim that it may
  be shared between threads.
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.ref_forming.{pub,priv}` -- `Deref`, `DerefMut`,
  `AsRef`, `AsMut`, `Borrow`, `BorrowMut`, `Index` and `IndexMut`, whose
  method returns a reference of a type the impl chose.
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.other.{pub,priv}` -- every other std trait:
  `Debug`, `PartialEq`, `Copy` and the rest.
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.local.{pub,priv}` -- the impls of a trait the crate
  declared itself: a shape it chose rather than adopted.
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.ffibox.layout.{pub,priv}` -- the impls of an ffibox
  trait that states a cell's layout or how it is reached and locked: the
  layout, seam and guard groups of [ffibox.md](ffibox.md#1-the-vocabulary).
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.ffibox.layout.of_which.<trait>.{handwritten,macro}` --
  those by trait, split by whether a generator wrote the impl rather than by
  visibility ([2.5](#25-deliberate-asymmetries)).
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.ffibox.policy.{pub,priv}` -- the impls of a lifecycle
  policy: the allocate, release and clone groups.
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.ffibox.policy.of_which.<trait>.{handwritten,macro}` --
  those by trait, likewise.
- `ty.generic.{pub,priv}` -- types carrying a generic parameter.
- `ty.generic.of_which.{lifetime,type}.{pub,priv}` -- of those, by kind of
  parameter. A lifetime ties the type to something it borrows; a type parameter
  makes it a family rather than one layout, so each instantiation is a separate
  question about C's bytes. A type may carry both.
- `ty.generic.of_which.storing_raw_ptr.{pub,priv}` -- the generic types that
  hold a raw pointer.
- `ty.field.ffibox.<primitive>.{pub,priv}` -- fields holding an ffibox
  primitive, by primitive: the delegation `ty.storing_raw_ptr` deliberately
  does not count as the crate's own pointer.
- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.{pub,priv}` -- the cell types: those that implement
  `CCell`.
- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.of_which.no_seam_trait.{pub,priv}` -- of those, the cells
  whose handles implement neither seam, so code generic over a handle has to
  special-case them.
- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.borrowed.std.{pub,priv}` -- MENTIONS of a cell in the
  crate's declarations, by what holds it: a cell named in twenty signatures is
  twenty of these. Here, the mentions behind a reference, which the convention
  says should be a handle instead.
- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.borrowed.std.of_which.{field,fn_sig}.{pub,priv}` -- of
  those, where they sit: a field's type, or a signature's. These two partition
  each arm of `as`.
- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.borrowed.std.of_which.self_in_ref_accessor.{pub,priv}`
  -- of the references, the receiver of an `as_ref` / `as_mut` accessor, which
  ffibox's contract licenses.
- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.borrowed.std.of_which.self_in_trait_impl.{pub,priv}` --
  the receiver of a trait impl's method, whose shape the trait fixed rather
  than the crate. The remainder of the references is the unsanctioned surface.
- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.borrowed.std.of_which.self_in_trait_impl.of_which.ref_forming.{pub,priv}`
  -- of those, the receivers of a `ref_forming` std trait's method, which
  returns a reference the impl chose.
- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.borrowed.ffibox.{pub,priv}` -- the mentions held by an
  ffibox borrow: `CBorrowedPtr`, `CSlice`, `CSliceMut`, `CGuardedRef`,
  `CGuard`.
- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.borrowed.ffibox.of_which.{field,fn_sig}.{pub,priv}` --
  where they sit.
- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.owned.std.{pub,priv}` -- the mentions held by a
  standard-library owner of its own storage (`Box`, `Vec`, a map).
- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.owned.std.of_which.{field,fn_sig}.{pub,priv}` -- where
  they sit.
- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.owned.ffibox.{pub,priv}` -- the mentions held by an
  ffibox owner: `CBox`, `CArc`, `CVec`, `CVal`.
- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.owned.ffibox.of_which.{field,fn_sig}.{pub,priv}` --
  where they sit.
- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.by_val.{pub,priv}` -- the mentions with nothing above
  them: the cell's bytes sit in the mention's own place.
- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.by_val.of_which.{field,fn_sig}.{pub,priv}` -- where
  they sit.
- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.fields.total` -- the crate's fns annotated as accessors
  of a C member: each `#[doc(alias = "<root>.<member>{.<member>}")]` whose
  member path resolves through the structs and unions the crates
  `--sys-crates` names declare, from a struct, a union or a type alias of one,
  once per alias and fn, so a getter and a setter of one member are two. The
  path names only what has a name: bindgen's `__bindgen_anon_<n>` members are
  looked through, a member bindgen escapes with a trailing `_` matches its C
  name, a bitfield resolves through the getter bindgen declares for it, and
  an array member continues into its element type. Only names are
  resolved, never layouts. Fns, not cells, so never summed into
  `ty.ffibox.wrapper`, and no `{pub,priv}`, like `ty.ffibox.sys`.
- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.fields.of_which.unique` -- the distinct member paths they
  name.
- `ty.ffibox.sys.total` -- the structs the crates `--sys-crates` names
  declare: the C aggregates the bindings expose. No `{pub,priv}`: they are
  another crate's types.
- `ty.ffibox.sys.of_which.raw_ptr_in_sys.total` -- of those, the ones a `-sys`
  declaration puts behind a raw pointer: a function's signature, a field, a
  callback typedef's parameters, or a member of a union a pointer reaches.
- `ty.ffibox.sys.of_which.raw_ptr_in_sys.of_which.used` -- of those, the ones
  the crate's compiled code names: in a declaration, or as the type of any
  expression or binding in a body.
- `ty.ffibox.sys.of_which.raw_ptr_in_sys.of_which.wrapped` -- of those, the ones
  a cell's `CCell::C` names.
- `ty.ffibox.sys.as.borrowed.std.{pub,priv}` -- the same mentions as
  `wrapper.as`'s, of the raw struct a cell covers, its `CCell::C`: the C layout
  named where the wrapper could have been.
- `ty.ffibox.sys.as.borrowed.std.of_which.{field,fn_sig}.{pub,priv}` -- as above.
- `ty.ffibox.sys.as.borrowed.std.of_which.{self_in_ref_accessor,self_in_trait_impl}.{pub,priv}`
  -- as above.
- `ty.ffibox.sys.as.borrowed.std.of_which.self_in_trait_impl.of_which.ref_forming.{pub,priv}`
  -- as above.
- `ty.ffibox.sys.as.borrowed.ffibox.{pub,priv}` -- as above.
- `ty.ffibox.sys.as.borrowed.ffibox.of_which.{field,fn_sig}.{pub,priv}` -- as
  above.
- `ty.ffibox.sys.as.owned.std.{pub,priv}` -- as above.
- `ty.ffibox.sys.as.owned.std.of_which.{field,fn_sig}.{pub,priv}` -- as above.
- `ty.ffibox.sys.as.owned.ffibox.{pub,priv}` -- as above.
- `ty.ffibox.sys.as.owned.ffibox.of_which.{field,fn_sig}.{pub,priv}` -- as above.
- `ty.ffibox.sys.as.by_val.{pub,priv}` -- as above.
- `ty.ffibox.sys.as.by_val.of_which.{field,fn_sig}.{pub,priv}` -- as above.

### 1.3 `fn`

Every function the crate defines, the methods of its trait impls included
([analysis 9.4](analysis.md#94-functions-and-methods)).

- `fn.total.{pub,priv}` -- the denominator, emitted: every function with a body.
- `fn.total.of_which.macro.{pub,priv}` -- of those, the ones a macro wrote.
  Subtract for the hand-written total.
- `fn.safe.{pub,priv}` -- the safe ones.
- `fn.safe.of_which.with_unsafe.{pub,priv}` -- of those, the ones whose body
  contains an `unsafe` block: a safe fn discharging an obligation internally.
  Counted on the safe arm only ([2.5](#25-deliberate-asymmetries)).
- `fn.unsafe.{pub,priv}` -- the `unsafe fn`s. `fn.unsafe.pub` is the unsafe
  surface a consumer meets.
- `fn.unsafe.of_which.in_trait_impl.std.{pub,priv}` -- of those, the methods
  of a trait impl, whose `unsafe` the trait's declaration fixed and the impl
  cannot drop: here, a standard-library trait's.
- `fn.unsafe.of_which.in_trait_impl.local.{pub,priv}` -- a trait the crate
  declared itself, which put the `unsafe` there one level up.
- `fn.unsafe.of_which.in_trait_impl.ffibox.{pub,priv}` -- an ffibox contract,
  such as `CDrop::c_drop`.
- `fn.unsafe.of_which.in_trait_impl.other.{pub,priv}` -- any other crate's
  trait.
- `fn.unsafe.of_which.seam.{pub,priv}` -- the `unsafe fn`s `--seams` names,
  which adopt a raw pointer by design. A seam may also be a trait's method, so
  this overlaps `in_trait_impl`.
- `fn.unsafe.of_which.other.{pub,priv}` -- the residual: neither a trait
  impl's method nor a seam, the `unsafe` the crate chose with nothing
  requiring it.
- `fn.unsafe.of_which.outside_regions.{pub,priv}` -- the `unsafe fn`s outside
  every module `--regions` named: the unsafe API the crate did not confine
  (safety).
- `fn.extern_abi.{pub,priv}` -- the fns the crate defines with a foreign ABI
  (`extern "C"`), which C reaches by symbol or by fn pointer (soundness).
- `fn.extern_abi.of_which.exported.{pub,priv}` -- of those, the ones carrying a
  C symbol name (`#[no_mangle]`, `#[export_name]`).
- `fn.extern_abi.of_which.macro.{pub,priv}` -- the ones a macro wrote.
- `fn.extern_abi.of_which.catches_unwind.{pub,priv}` -- the ones whose body
  calls `std::panic::catch_unwind`, a fn `--barriers` named, or, under
  `--ffibox`, ffibox's `callback::barrier`: a panic stopped before it unwinds
  into C. The rest is read by subtracting (soundness).
- `fn.extern_abi.of_which.raw_ptr_sig.{pub,priv}` -- the ones whose signature
  holds a raw pointer.
- `fn.extern_abi.of_which.ffibox_sig.{pub,priv}` -- the ones whose signature
  holds an ffibox primitive, an owner or handle in place of a pointer.
- `fn.extern_abi.of_which.ffibox_macro.{pub,priv}` -- the ones an ffibox macro
  wrote, such as its `export_*!` lifecycle exports.
- `fn.sig.of_which.c_type.{arg,ret}.{pub,priv}` -- mentions of C's types in
  the signatures the crate chose, a trait impl's methods left out: C's scalar
  names (`c_int`, `c_char`, and `libc`'s), read from the signature as written
  since typeck erases them, and foreign-ABI fn pointers. What a consumer of a
  Rust API handles in C's terms (ergonomics).
- `fn.sig.of_which.result.ret.{pub,priv}` -- the fns, trait impls' methods
  left out, that return a `Result`: failure in Rust's vocabulary rather than
  C's status codes (idiomaticity).
- `fn.sig.of_which.ffibox.{arg,ret}.<primitive>.{pub,priv}` -- mentions of an
  ffibox primitive in a signature, by position and by primitive, the ones
  inside a `Result`, an `Option` or a reference included
  ([analysis 9.4](analysis.md#94-functions-and-methods)): whether the
  vocabulary actually crosses the interface.
- `fn.ffibox.sys.total` -- the fns the crates `--sys-crates` names declare,
  and those of the scanned crate's own modules it names as `crate::<path>`:
  the C functions the bindings expose, macro shims included. No `{pub,priv}`:
  they are another crate's.
- `fn.ffibox.sys.of_which.used` -- of those, the ones the crate's compiled code
  names, by calling one or coercing it to a pointer.
- `fn.ffibox.wrapper.{non_trait,other_trait}` -- the crate's fns annotated as
  wrappers of a C function: each `#[doc(alias)]` naming a fn of the `-sys`
  crates, once per alias and fn, so the variants a C function is forked into
  count once each. By where the annotated fn sits: a free fn or an inherent
  method (`non_trait`), or the method of a trait that is no ffibox policy
  (`other_trait`). No `{pub,priv}`, like `fn.ffibox.sys`.
- `fn.ffibox.wrapper.policy.<trait>` -- the method of an ffibox lifecycle
  policy, such as `CDrop::c_drop`, by trait: the allocate, release and clone
  groups of [ffibox.md](ffibox.md#1-the-vocabulary).
- `fn.ffibox.wrapper.of_which.unique` -- the distinct C functions they name.

### 1.4 `static`

The statics the crate defines; an `extern` block's declarations are C's.

- `static.total.{pub,priv}` -- every static the crate defines. Emitted, and the
  denominator its shares are read against.
- `static.of_which.mut.{pub,priv}` -- the `static mut`s: shared mutable state
  no borrow checks (soundness).
- `static.of_which.exported.{pub,priv}` -- the ones carrying a C symbol name,
  which C reads by that name (soundness).

### 1.5 `code`

The size of the crate and what its bodies do, as the denominators the rest is
read against.

- `code.loc.total` -- lines of code, from the compiled crate: the union of HIR
  definition spans, blanks and comments excluded, so items `cfg` removed are
  not in the denominator.
- `code.loc.unsafe` -- of those, the lines inside an `unsafe` block, filtered
  the same way so the two are comparable.
- `code.unsafe_block.total` -- `unsafe` blocks, however many lines each holds.
- `code.unsafe_block.of_which.ffi_export` -- of those, the ones inside a fn
  that is the C-ABI boundary: one with a foreign ABI or a C symbol name, or a
  closure inside one ([analysis 9.7](analysis.md#97-regions-and-the-c-abi-boundary)).
- `code.unsafe_block.of_which.region.<region>` -- the ones inside a module

  ([analysis 9.6](analysis.md#96-test-code)).

- `code.tests.fn` -- functions in the test code, including one generated
  harness `main` per test binary.

## 2. The shape of a record

### 2.1 Partitions and shares

A partition's children are disjoint and sum to it; an `of_which` node's
children are subsets that overlap and are never summed. `nest_ptr` derives
every partition `total` bottom-up and skips `of_which` when summing, so no sum
is written by the driver and none can disagree with its parts.

`ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which` is a share family: a type may implement both
`Drop` and `Clone`, so its arms overlap and only the record itself is a
population. An `of_which` node therefore carries no `total` of its own --
summing two shares is not a quantity -- while each share keeps the total of its
own `{pub,priv}` partition. A share may refine another share, and then it nests
under it: `fn_sig_trait_impl.of_which.ffibox.of_which.<trait>` is the ffibox
positions by trait.

One child is of another unit: `as` holds the mentions of the types its parent
counts -- `ty.ffibox.wrapper` is the cell types, `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as` the
places they are named -- so it is never summed into the parent either, while
it is a record with a total of its own, which its arms partition. So is
`ty.ffibox.wrapper.fields`, the fns annotated as field accessors on those
cells.

Where a residual is wanted it is emitted as a share named for it --
`ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.none`, `ty.total.of_which.no_trait` -- rather than
left for a reader to subtract.

### 2.2 Namespaces

Three kinds of node carry no derived `total`: an `of_which` node, as above; a
node that already carries an emitted one, which is how the denominators
`raw_ptr.total`, `ty.total` and `code.loc.total` survive a derivation that
would otherwise take their name; and a NAMESPACE, a node whose children are
families rather than the parts of one quantity.

A top-level prefix is always a namespace -- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg` counts
signature positions and `raw_ptr.deref` counts body sites, so their sum means
nothing -- and four are namespaces a level down. `ty.ffibox` holds two type
counts, the cells (`wrapper`) and the `-sys` crates' types (`sys`), each with
its mentions under `as`. `code.tests` holds four separate
measurements of the test build: its lines, its unsafe lines -- a subset of them
-- its unsafe blocks and its fns; their sum read 103840 on libgit2-bindings, a
figure with no unit at all. `fn.sig` holds what a signature carries, in
mentions -- a fn taking two `CBox` is two of them -- so it is a share of no
count of fns, and `fn.total` beside it is the denominator a reader divides by.
Its own arms do carry totals: `fn.sig.of_which.ffibox` is `arg` plus `ret`,
which are disjoint. `fn.ffibox` holds two fn counts as `ty.ffibox` holds two
type counts: the crate's annotated wrappers (`wrapper`) and the `-sys` crates'
fns (`sys`).

`nest_ptr` declares them in `NAMESPACES` rather than inferring them, since no
shape distinguishes a namespace from a partition: `raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg`'s
`{safe,unsafe}` children are records with their own totals too, and summing
those is exactly right.

### 2.3 Zero, and absent

Every counter the invocation's flags turn on is in the document, at `0` when
it never fired. A reader of one document cannot tell an absent counter from
one the schema does not have -- no `owned.std` under `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as`
could mean "no cell is held in a std collection" or "that arm was never
written" --
and the schema is too long to hold in the head, so the driver registers every
path it can emit before the passes run and they count up from there.

What is absent is what the flags did not turn on, which is a different
statement and a deliberate one: the ffibox arms without `--ffibox`, and the
`of_which.seam` shares without `--seams`. A `0` there would say the scan
looked and found none, when it did not look.

The registry is in the driver, beside the passes, and it iterates the same
vocabulary lists they do, so the trait and primitive arms cannot drift from
it. `RegistryTests` reads the registry off a scan of
`tests/fixtures/empty/` -- a crate with nothing in it, whose every counter is
therefore 0 -- and holds the other fixtures' fired counters to it.

### 2.4 The order of a record

A record's children are written in a declared order, most salient first: the
record's own `total`, then the splits it is cut by (`unsafe` before `safe`,
`pub` before `priv`), then its families, then its shares and arms, and
`of_which` last, since a share is read against the partition it cuts across.
The prefixes come in this document's order: `raw_ptr`, `ty`, `fn`, `code`.

The driver emits a sorted map, so the alternative is alphabetical: `fn` would
read `{safe, sig, total, unsafe}`, with the denominator in the middle.

A name the order does not hold comes after every name it does, alphabetically.
That is where the primitive arms land -- `CArc`, `CBorrowedPtr`, `CBox` -- so a
primitive added to ffibox needs no change to the order and still reads
predictably. The trait arms are declared, in the order
[`ffibox.md`](ffibox.md) gives the vocabulary, so a breakdown by trait reads as
the lifecycle it describes rather than alphabetically.
`measure.KEY_ORDER` is one table for every level, since a name that earns an
early rank in one record earns it in the
