414	## 2. The shape of a record
415	
416	### 2.1 Partitions and shares
417	
418	A partition's children are disjoint and sum to it; an `of_which` node's
419	children are subsets that overlap and are never summed. `nest_ptr` derives
420	every partition `total` bottom-up and skips `of_which` when summing, so no sum
421	is written by the driver and none can disagree with its parts.
422	
423	`ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which` is a share family: a type may implement both
424	`Drop` and `Clone`, so its arms overlap and only the record itself is a
425	population. An `of_which` node therefore carries no `total` of its own --
426	summing two shares is not a quantity -- while each share keeps the total of its
427	own `{pub,priv}` partition. A share may refine another share, and then it nests
428	under it: `fn_sig_trait_impl.of_which.ffibox.of_which.<trait>` is the ffibox
429	positions by trait.
430	
431	One child is of another unit: `as` holds the mentions of the types its parent
432	counts -- `ty.ffibox.wrapper` is the cell types, `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as` the
433	places they are named -- so it is never summed into the parent either, while
434	it is a record with a total of its own, which its arms partition. So is
435	`ty.ffibox.wrapper.fields`, the fns annotated as field accessors on those
436	cells.
437	
438	Where a residual is wanted it is emitted as a share named for it --
439	`ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.none`, `ty.total.of_which.no_trait` -- rather than
440	left for a reader to subtract.
441	
442	### 2.2 Namespaces
443	
444	Three kinds of node carry no derived `total`: an `of_which` node, as above; a
445	node that already carries an emitted one, which is how the denominators
446	`raw_ptr.total`, `ty.total` and `code.loc.total` survive a derivation that
447	would otherwise take their name; and a NAMESPACE, a node whose children are
448	families rather than the parts of one quantity.
449	
450	A top-level prefix is always a namespace -- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg` counts
451	signature positions and `raw_ptr.deref` counts body sites, so their sum means
452	nothing -- and four are namespaces a level down. `ty.ffibox` holds two type
453	counts, the cells (`wrapper`) and the `-sys` crates' types (`sys`), each with
454	its mentions under `as`. `code.tests` holds four separate
455	measurements of the test build: its lines, its unsafe lines -- a subset of them
456	-- its unsafe blocks and its fns; their sum read 103840 on libgit2-bindings, a
457	figure with no unit at all. `fn.sig` holds what a signature carries, in
458	mentions -- a fn taking two `CBox` is two of them -- so it is a share of no
459	count of fns, and `fn.total` beside it is the denominator a reader divides by.
460	Its own arms do carry totals: `fn.sig.of_which.ffibox` is `arg` plus `ret`,
461	which are disjoint. `fn.ffibox` holds two fn counts as `ty.ffibox` holds two
462	type counts: the crate's annotated wrappers (`wrapper`) and the `-sys` crates'
463	fns (`sys`).
464	
465	`nest_ptr` declares them in `NAMESPACES` rather than inferring them, since no
466	shape distinguishes a namespace from a partition: `raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg`'s
467	`{safe,unsafe}` children are records with their own totals too, and summing
468	those is exactly right.
469	
470	### 2.3 Zero, and absent
471	
472	Every counter the invocation's flags turn on is in the document, at `0` when
473	it never fired. A reader of one document cannot tell an absent counter from
474	one the schema does not have -- no `owned.std` under `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as`
475	could mean "no cell is held in a std collection" or "that arm was never
476	written" --
477	and the schema is too long to hold in the head, so the driver registers every
478	path it can emit before the passes run and they count up from there.
479	
480	What is absent is what the flags did not turn on, which is a different
481	statement and a deliberate one: the ffibox arms without `--ffibox`, and the
482	`of_which.seam` shares without `--seams`. A `0` there would say the scan
483	looked and found none, when it did not look.
484	
485	The registry is in the driver, beside the passes, and it iterates the same
486	vocabulary lists they do, so the trait and primitive arms cannot drift from
487	it. `RegistryTests` reads the registry off a scan of
488	`tests/fixtures/empty/` -- a crate with nothing in it, whose every counter is
489	therefore 0 -- and holds the other fixtures' fired counters to it.
490	
491	### 2.4 The order of a record
492	
493	A record's children are written in a declared order, most salient first: the
494	record's own `total`, then the splits it is cut by (`unsafe` before `safe`,
495	`pub` before `priv`), then its families, then its shares and arms, and
496	`of_which` last, since a share is read against the partition it cuts across.
497	The prefixes come in this document's order: `raw_ptr`, `ty`, `fn`, `code`.
498	
499	The driver emits a sorted map, so the alternative is alphabetical: `fn` would
500	read `{safe, sig, total, unsafe}`, with the denominator in the middle.
501	
502	A name the order does not hold comes after every name it does, alphabetically.
503	That is where the primitive arms land -- `CArc`, `CBorrowedPtr`, `CBox` -- so a
504	primitive added to ffibox needs no change to the order and still reads
505	predictably. The trait arms are declared, in the order
506	[`ffibox.md`](ffibox.md) gives the vocabulary, so a breakdown by trait reads as
507	the lifecycle it describes rather than alphabetically.
508	`measure.KEY_ORDER` is one table for every level, since a name that earns an
509	early rank in one record earns it in the others: `unsafe` is early as
510	`fn.unsafe`, as `code.loc.unsafe` and as the unsafe trait impls. `fn` is the
511	one name it cannot place for every record, being a prefix as well as one of
512	`code.tests`'s measurements, so it is ranked for the latter. A type count's
513	`as` comes after its `of_which`, since the mentions are read once the types
514	are.
515	
516	### 2.5 Deliberate asymmetries
517	
518	A split that is not carried where a reader might expect it, and why.
519	
520	`ty.impl_trait.of_which.ffibox.{layout,policy}.of_which.<trait>` splits
521	`{handwritten,macro}` but not `{pub,priv}`: whether a generator was used does
522	not vary with visibility, and the split would cost a cell per trait for
523	nothing.
524	
525	`raw_ptr.fn_sig_trait_impl.of_which.ffibox.of_which.<trait>` splits by neither:
526	a trait method's safety and visibility are the trait declaration's, one
527	spelling dictating every impl, so the split would restate the parent cell by
528	cell. The parent `ffibox` arm carries both, since the mix of traits a crate
529	implements does move them.
530	
531	`fn.safe.of_which.with_unsafe` is counted on the safe arm only. With
532	`unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn` denied, every `unsafe fn` doing anything raw has a
533	block by construction, so counting it there would measure the lint.
534	
535	`raw_ptr.fn_sig_trait_impl` carries no direction, while `fn_sig_arg` and
536	`fn_sig_ret` are separate counters: the direction says what the crate chose to
537	do with the pointer, and in a trait impl it chose neither.
538	
539	## 3. Building a report
540	
541	A report is leaves divided and subtracted, named by their paths. Three rules
542	make the arithmetic sound:
543	
544	- a partition may be summed, an `of_which` may not, and an `as` never with the
545	  types above it. Two shares of one record overlap, so
546	  `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.impl_drop + impl_clone` is not a quantity, while
547	  `pub + priv` is the record;
548	- a rate stays inside one record, or between a record and the denominator
549	  emitted for it: `fn.unsafe.pub / fn.total.pub`, `code.loc.unsafe /
550	  code.loc.total`, `ty.storing_raw_ptr.pub / ty.total.pub`. Dividing across
551	  prefixes mixes grains -- signature positions by lines of code says nothing;
552	- a share is read against the record it cuts, and the remainder is a
553	  subtraction: `wrapper.as.borrowed.std.pub` less its two sanctioned shares is
554	  the convention's unsanctioned surface.
555	
556	### 3.1 The readings worth taking
557	
558	Each reading below names the leaves it is made of. The figures are not here: a
559	reading of one crate is in [`analysis.md`](analysis.md), where it is the
560	evidence for a rule, and a reading of several is in
561	[`examples/README.md`](../examples/README.md), where three real documents are
562	tabulated side by side. A figure copied into this document would be a second
563	copy to keep current, and the counters are what this document is for.
564	
565	**How much of the bindings has a cell.** Under `--ffibox` with the `-sys`
566	crates named, `ty.ffibox.sys.of_which.raw_ptr_in_sys.of_which.wrapped` against
567	`raw_ptr_in_sys` is the share of the C types the bindings hand around by pointer
568	that the crate has given a cell, and `used` against it the share the crate
569	touches at all, so the gap between the two shares is the C it touches
570	without a cell ([ffibox.md](ffibox.md#8-where-the-declarations-mention-a-cell)). Against `ty.ffibox.sys.total` it reads low by
571	construction, since a by-value struct needs no cell.
572	
573	**How much of the C functions has a wrapper.** Under `--ffibox` with the
574	`-sys` crates named, `fn.ffibox.wrapper.of_which.unique` against
575	`fn.ffibox.sys.total` is the share of the C functions the bindings declare
576	that the crate annotates a wrapper for, and `fn.ffibox.sys.of_which.used`
577	against it the share it calls at all. The annotation is the only record of
578	what a wrapper wraps, so an unannotated wrapper reads as none; the alias is
579	the one the Crustify conventions require. `fn.ffibox.wrapper.total` against
580	`unique` is how many variants a wrapped function was forked into on average.
581	
582	**Which `unsafe fn`s nothing required.** `fn.unsafe.of_which.other` is the
583	unsafe surface the crate chose: no trait declared the method unsafe and no
584	seam adopts a pointer through it. Read it against `fn.unsafe`, and its `pub`
585	leaf against `fn.unsafe.pub`, rather than subtracting `in_trait_impl` and
586	`seam`, which overlap.
587	
588	**What a consumer meets without writing `unsafe`.**
589	`raw_ptr.total.safe.pub` is the raw pointers on the safe public interface,
590	`fn.unsafe.pub` against `fn.total.pub` the public unsafe surface, and
591	`raw_ptr.field.pub` the pointers a public field hands over with no `unsafe` at
592	all.
593	
594	**How much unsafe, and where it sits.** `code.loc.unsafe / code.loc.total` is
595	the density and `code.unsafe_block.total` the number of blocks; read both,
596	since folding small blocks into large ones moves one and not the other.
597	`code.unsafe_block.of_which.ffi_export` subtracts the gateways a port campaign
598	generated, and the `code.unsafe_call` arms say what the unsafe is for: `ffi`
599	is the boundary, `rust` is the standard library's constructors and the crate's
600	own helpers, `intrinsic` is `transmute` and its siblings.
601	
602	**What the crate wrote, as opposed to what a macro did.** Subtract
603	`fn.total.of_which.macro` from `fn.total`, and
604	`ty.impl_trait.of_which.derived` from `ty.impl_trait`. A comparison of two
605	crates without those shares is partly a comparison of how much boilerplate
606	each spells.
607	
608	**What the crate declares about the pointers it manages.**
609	`ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.none` against `ty.storing_raw_ptr` is the types
610	that hold a pointer and say nothing about it. The other shares say what the
611	rest declared -- `impl_drop`, `impl_clone`, `ffibox` -- and `pub_field` is the
612	opposite of a declaration.
613	
614	**Whether a convention is kept.** Under `--ffibox`,
615	`ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.borrowed.std` less `self_in_ref_accessor` and
616	`self_in_trait_impl` is the bare `&Foo` surface the convention says should be a
617	handle. `as.owned.std` and `as.by_val` against `as.owned.ffibox` say how much
618	of a cell's storage the crate holds itself rather than through ffibox's
619	owners. `ty.ffibox.wrapper.of_which.no_seam_trait` is the cells a generic
620	handle has to special-case, and `fn.sig.of_which.ffibox` whether the
621	vocabulary reaches the interface at all.
622	
623	**What the trait impls do.** `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std`'s arms say which of
624	the crate's adopted traits act on what it wraps: `drop` and `clone` run its
625	lifecycle, `send` and `sync` are claims about threads, `ref_forming` can hand
626	out a reference to it. Under `--ffibox`, `ty.impl_trait.of_which.ffibox`'s
627	`layout` and `policy` say how much of the convention is the cells' layout and
628	how much their lifecycle.
629	
630	**Whose shape the pointers in trait impls are.** `fn_sig_trait_impl` is read
631	through its `of_which` arms, never bare: one crate's are a convention's
632	lifecycle strategies, another's its own private helpers, a third's one local
633	conversion trait, and the bare figure is the same for all three.
634	
635	**The test code, beside the library and never added to it.**
636	`code.tests.loc.total` against `code.loc.total` is how much of the tree is
637	tests, and the `code.tests` arms are the only counters that include them.
638	
639	A report of several crates is a table of leaves, one row per crate, with the
640	denominator beside every share.
641	
642	### 3.2 What a comparison requires
643	
644	The document is a pure function of the source tree under a fixed scanner, so
645	two figures are comparable only when the scanner and the flags match: the
646	ffimap commit, the toolchain, `--sys-crates` (which decides what
647	`ty.storing_raw_ptr` admits), `--seams` (which decides what the `seam` shares
648	and `casted_to.local_seam` can see) and any framework the crate is built on.
649	The `scanner` and `sys_crates` fields carry all of it, which is why they are in
650	the document rather than beside it. `scanner.ffimap` names one scanner only as
651	a commit, bare or with the hash of its uncommitted changes: a package version
652	is what every copy outside a checkout of its own records, so `ffimap diff`
653	reports two such documents as under scanners not known to be the same
654	([analysis 1](analysis.md#1-determinism-and-what-it-rests-on)).
655	
656	A counter added or a rule corrected moves figures too. The ones already known
657	to be incomparable across versions are named in
658	[analysis 12](analysis.md#12-what-the-analysis-cannot-see).
659	
660	### 3.3 No target values
661	
662	ffimap has none, and this is the place that says so. Absolute counts are not
663	comparable across crates of different size, and lower is not automatically
664	better: a wrapper over C must contain unsafe, and folding 600 small audited
665	blocks into 200 large ones improves the number while making the crate worse.
666	A reader who wants a rate divides the leaves it names.
667	
668	Finding what is worth looking at is the opposite kind of work, and belongs to
669	a reviewer who reads the code, forms suspicions and defends them. `none` and
670	`no_seam_trait` name an absence, not a defect.
671

# Counter schema

The counters ffimap reports: what each one holds, how a record is shaped, and
how a report is built from them. Every counter is determined from declarations
and single expression nodes -- no value is followed, no cast chain is composed,
and no dataflow is performed.

What each counter is decided FROM, and how a scan runs, is
[`analysis.md`](analysis.md); the ffibox vocabulary the `<trait>` and
`<primitive>` arms are generated from is [`ffibox.md`](ffibox.md).

## 1. The counters

Each row below is one counter, named by its dotted path into the document's
`counts`. A `{a,b}` is a split the counter carries: `raw_ptr.field.{pub,priv}`
is two leaves, and every row's leaves are integers. Each partition also carries
a `total`, derived from its children unless the driver emits it, so
`raw_ptr.field.total` exists and `raw_ptr.field.pub + raw_ptr.field.priv`
equals it; the `of_which` rows are shares of the row above them and are never
summed ([2.1](#21-partitions-and-shares)).

The counters are the whole of the document's `counts`. There is no second,
flat counter block beside them, and no prose rendering of them: a reader who
wants a rate divides the leaves it names.

Across the tree, `unsafe` and `safe` are the safety of the *function* the
position or site is in, `pub` and `priv` whether a consumer of the crate can
reach the item, and `void` a pointer whose pointee is erased (`*c_void`). A row
naming `ffibox`, a `<trait>` or a `<primitive>` is present only under
`--ffibox`, an `of_which.seam` row only with `--seams`, and a `region` or
`outside_regions` row only with `--regions`; each is absent rather than zero
otherwise ([2.3](#23-zero-and-absent)). A row ends with the property it bears
on, as [goals.md](goals.md) names them: safety, soundness, ergonomics or
idiomaticity.

### 1.1 `raw_ptr`

The raw pointers the crate declares in its signatures and types, and what its
bodies do with them.

- `raw_ptr.total.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- the denominator: every
  raw-pointer position the crate CHOSE, which is `fn_sig_arg` plus
  `fn_sig_ret` plus `field`. Emitted rather than derived, so it is not a sum of
  the families beside it ([analysis 9.2](analysis.md#92-what-raw_ptrtotal-admits)).
- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- raw pointers an argument of
  a signature takes. Taking is the hazard: a safe fn that takes one lets a
  caller pass anything with no `unsafe` at the call site.
- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg.of_which.void.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- of those, the
  erased ones. Subtract the share for the typed ones.
- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg.of_which.seam.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- of those, the
  ones in a function `--seams` declared to be nothing but a conversion between
  a wrapper and its raw pointer.
- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_ret.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- raw pointers a signature
  returns. Returning one still forces the caller to write `unsafe` before it
  means anything, which is why it is counted apart from `fn_sig_arg`.
- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_ret.of_which.void.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- as above.
- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_ret.of_which.seam.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- as above.
- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_trait_impl.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- positions in a trait
  impl's method, both directions in one counter: a trait declaration fixed the
  signature, so the crate did not choose the position, and the figure would
  otherwise move with how many types a trait is implemented for
  ([analysis 9.3](analysis.md#93-positions-a-trait-fixed)).
- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_trait_impl.of_which.void.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- as above.
- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_trait_impl.of_which.seam.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- as above.
- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_trait_impl.of_which.std.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- of
  those, the ones a standard-library trait fixed.
- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_trait_impl.of_which.local.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- the
  ones a trait the crate declared itself fixed.
- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_trait_impl.of_which.ffibox.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- the
  ones an ffibox contract fixed, which for a crate built on the convention is
  its lifecycle strategies.
- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_trait_impl.of_which.ffibox.of_which.<trait>` -- those by
  trait, over the whole vocabulary, so a document says which contracts reach a
  raw pointer and which do not. No safety or visibility split: a trait method's
  are the declaration's ([2.5](#25-deliberate-asymmetries)).
- `raw_ptr.field.{pub,priv}` -- struct and union fields declared with a raw
  pointer. `pub` is one reachability question, the type exported AND the field
  exported, rather than two levels a reader has to combine.
- `raw_ptr.field.of_which.void.{pub,priv}` -- of those, the erased ones.
- `raw_ptr.deref.{rd,wr}` -- dereference sites in bodies, by whether the place
  is read or written. Sites, not positions, so they are outside `raw_ptr.total`.
- `raw_ptr.casted_to.std.{owner,string,borrow,slice,other}` -- a raw pointer
  converted into a standard-library shape, by the shape it became: an owner
  (`Box`, `Vec`, `Rc`, `Arc`), a string (`CStr`, `CString`, `String`), a
  borrow, a slice. `other` is a shape the table does not know, which for `std`
  is none of them ([analysis 11.3](analysis.md#113-other)).
- `raw_ptr.casted_to.ffibox.{owner,string,borrow,slice}` -- adopted into an
  ffibox primitive, by the primitive's group. There is no `other` arm: every
  primitive maps to a shape.
- `raw_ptr.casted_to.local_seam.{owner,string,borrow,slice,other}` -- converted
  through a function `--seams` named, by the seam's return type. `other` is a
  seam returning a bespoke handle.
- `raw_ptr.surrendered.std.{owner,string}` -- the other direction: a value
  Rust owns turned into a raw pointer by a standard-library call, such as
  `Box::into_raw` or `CString::into_raw`, by the shape it had. What C is then
  trusted to give back to the allocator that made it (soundness).
- `raw_ptr.surrendered.ffibox.<shape>` -- the same through an ffibox
  primitive's `into_raw`, `into_c` or `into_raw_parts`, by the primitive's
  shape, as `casted_to.ffibox` reads it (soundness).

### 1.2 `ty`

The types the crate defines, by what they hold and what they declare about it.

- `ty.total.{pub,priv}` -- every type the crate defines. Emitted, and the
  denominator its shares are read against.
- `ty.total.of_which.std_trait.{pub,priv}` -- of those, the types that
  implement a standard-library trait.
- `ty.total.of_which.local_trait.{pub,priv}` -- the types that implement a
  trait the crate declared itself.
- `ty.total.of_which.ffibox_trait.{pub,priv}` -- the types that implement an
  ffibox contract.
- `ty.total.of_which.no_trait.{pub,priv}` -- the residual: types that
  implement no trait at all.
- `ty.total.of_which.macro.{pub,priv}` -- the types a macro wrote, such as
  `bitflags!`'s: subtract for the hand-written ones, as for `fn.total`.
- `ty.total.of_which.{repr_c,repr_transparent}.{pub,priv}` -- the types whose
  layout is C's (`#[repr(C)]`) or exactly another type's
  (`#[repr(transparent)]`): the layouts the crate shares with C (soundness).
- `ty.total.of_which.std_impl.<trait>.{pub,priv}` -- the types that implement
  one of a fixed list of std traits a Rust consumer expects of a value, by
  trait: `Debug`, `Display`, `Error`, `Clone`, `Default`, `PartialEq`, `Eq`,
  `Hash`, `Iterator` and `From`, derived or written (idiomaticity).
- `ty.storing_raw_ptr.{pub,priv}` -- types whose fields reach a raw pointer,
  within the peel set, so these are the types that manage one themselves
  rather than delegating to `Vec` or to an ffibox owner
  ([analysis 9.1](analysis.md#91-the-peel-set)).
- `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.impl_drop.{pub,priv}` -- of those, the ones that
  implement `Drop`: they free memory Rust did not allocate.
- `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.impl_clone.{pub,priv}` -- the ones that
  implement `Clone`, where a shallow clone duplicates the pointer and, with
  `Drop`, double-frees it.
- `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.{impl_deref,impl_deref_mut}.{pub,priv}` -- the
  ones that hand out a reference derived from the pointer implicitly, at every
  call site.
- `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.impl_send_sync.{pub,priv}` -- the ones that
  assert thread safety for memory no type system checked.
- `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.has_lifetime.{pub,priv}` -- the ones that tie
  the pointer to a lifetime parameter.
- `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.ffibox.{pub,priv}` -- the ones that declare
  their lifecycle through an ffibox contract, which none of the std shares can
  see.
- `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.pub_field.{pub,priv}` -- the ones that publish
  the pointer as a public field. Not a declaration: an access the type does not
  govern.
- `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.none.{pub,priv}` -- the residual: the type
  stores a pointer and declares nothing about it, in any vocabulary.
- `ty.wrapping_unsafe_cell.{pub,priv}` -- types holding an `UnsafeCell`, the
  one way to hold a value C may write while Rust holds a shared reference to it.
- `ty.impl_block.{pub,priv}` -- inherent `impl T` blocks: the API the crate
  wrote for its own type.
- `ty.impl_block.of_which.ffibox.{layout,ref,mut,locked}.{pub,priv}` -- of
  those, the blocks on a cell and on each of its handles, which are different
  surfaces: the layout type carries the constructors, the shared handle the
  getters, the exclusive handle the setters.
- `ty.impl_block.of_which.other.{pub,priv}` -- the blocks on everything else.
- `ty.impl_trait.{pub,priv}` -- `impl Tr for T` blocks: satisfying someone
  else's shape.
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.unsafe` -- of those, the `unsafe impl`s, which assert
  what the compiler cannot check. `TrivialClone`, which `#[derive(Clone)]`
  emits, is skipped.
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.derived.{pub,priv}` -- the ones a `#[derive]` wrote.
  Nobody typed them, and they are most of the `std` arm.
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.drop.{pub,priv}` -- the impls of a
  standard-library trait, by trait: `Drop`, which runs code when an object is
  released.
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.clone.{pub,priv}` -- `Clone`, which duplicates
  one.
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.send.{pub,priv}` -- `Send`, the claim that an
  object may move to another thread.
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.sync.{pub,priv}` -- `Sync`, the claim that it may
  be shared between threads.
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.ref_forming.{pub,priv}` -- `Deref`, `DerefMut`,
  `AsRef`, `AsMut`, `Borrow`, `BorrowMut`, `Index` and `IndexMut`, whose
  method returns a reference of a type the impl chose.
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.other.{pub,priv}` -- every other std trait:
  `Debug`, `PartialEq`, `Copy` and the rest.
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.local.{pub,priv}` -- the impls of a trait the crate
  declared itself: a shape it chose rather than adopted.
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.ffibox.layout.{pub,priv}` -- the impls of an ffibox
  trait that states a cell's layout or how it is reached and locked: the
  layout, seam and guard groups of [ffibox.md](ffibox.md#1-the-vocabulary).
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.ffibox.layout.of_which.<trait>.{handwritten,macro}` --
  those by trait, split by whether a generator wrote the impl rather than by
  visibility ([2.5](#25-deliberate-asymmetries)).
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.ffibox.policy.{pub,priv}` -- the impls of a lifecycle
  policy: the allocate, release and clone groups.
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.ffibox.policy.of_which.<trait>.{handwritten,macro}` --
  those by trait, likewise.
- `ty.generic.{pub,priv}` -- types carrying a generic parameter.
- `ty.generic.of_which.{lifetime,type}.{pub,priv}` -- of those, by kind of
  parameter. A lifetime ties the type to something it borrows; a type parameter
  makes it a family rather than one layout, so each instantiation is a separate
  question about C's bytes. A type may carry both.
- `ty.generic.of_which.storing_raw_ptr.{pub,priv}` -- the generic types that
  hold a raw pointer.
- `ty.field.ffibox.<primitive>.{pub,priv}` -- fields holding an ffibox
  primitive, by primitive: the delegation `ty.storing_raw_ptr` deliberately
  does not count as the crate's own pointer.
- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.{pub,priv}` -- the cell types: those that implement
  `CCell`.
- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.of_which.no_seam_trait.{pub,priv}` -- of those, the cells
  whose handles implement neither seam, so code generic over a handle has to
  special-case them.
- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.borrowed.std.{pub,priv}` -- MENTIONS of a cell in the
  crate's declarations, by what holds it: a cell named in twenty signatures is
  twenty of these. Here, the mentions behind a reference, which the convention
  says should be a handle instead.
- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.borrowed.std.of_which.{field,fn_sig}.{pub,priv}` -- of
  those, where they sit: a field's type, or a signature's. These two partition
  each arm of `as`.
- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.borrowed.std.of_which.self_in_ref_accessor.{pub,priv}`
  -- of the references, the receiver of an `as_ref` / `as_mut` accessor, which
  ffibox's contract licenses.
- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.borrowed.std.of_which.self_in_trait_impl.{pub,priv}` --
  the receiver of a trait impl's method, whose shape the trait fixed rather
  than the crate. The remainder of the references is the unsanctioned surface.
- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.borrowed.std.of_which.self_in_trait_impl.of_which.ref_forming.{pub,priv}`
  -- of those, the receivers of a `ref_forming` std trait's method, which
  returns a reference the impl chose.
- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.borrowed.ffibox.{pub,priv}` -- the mentions held by an
  ffibox borrow: `CBorrowedPtr`, `CSlice`, `CSliceMut`, `CGuardedRef`,
  `CGuard`.
- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.borrowed.ffibox.of_which.{field,fn_sig}.{pub,priv}` --
  where they sit.
- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.owned.std.{pub,priv}` -- the mentions held by a
  standard-library owner of its own storage (`Box`, `Vec`, a map).
- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.owned.std.of_which.{field,fn_sig}.{pub,priv}` -- where
  they sit.
- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.owned.ffibox.{pub,priv}` -- the mentions held by an
  ffibox owner: `CBox`, `CArc`, `CVec`, `CVal`.
- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.owned.ffibox.of_which.{field,fn_sig}.{pub,priv}` --
  where they sit.
- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.by_val.{pub,priv}` -- the mentions with nothing above
  them: the cell's bytes sit in the mention's own place.
- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.by_val.of_which.{field,fn_sig}.{pub,priv}` -- where
  they sit.
- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.fields.total` -- the crate's fns annotated as accessors
  of a C member: each `#[doc(alias = "<root>.<member>{.<member>}")]` whose
  member path resolves through the structs and unions the crates
  `--sys-crates` names declare, from a struct, a union or a type alias of one,
  once per alias and fn, so a getter and a setter of one member are two. The
  path names only what has a name: bindgen's `__bindgen_anon_<n>` members are
  looked through, a member bindgen escapes with a trailing `_` matches its C
  name, a bitfield resolves through the getter bindgen declares for it, and
  an array member continues into its element type. Only names are
  resolved, never layouts. Fns, not cells, so never summed into
  `ty.ffibox.wrapper`, and no `{pub,priv}`, like `ty.ffibox.sys`.
- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.fields.of_which.unique` -- the distinct member paths they
  name.
- `ty.ffibox.sys.total` -- the structs the crates `--sys-crates` names
  declare: the C aggregates the bindings expose. No `{pub,priv}`: they are
  another crate's types.
- `ty.ffibox.sys.of_which.raw_ptr_in_sys.total` -- of those, the ones a `-sys`
  declaration puts behind a raw pointer: a function's signature, a field, a
  callback typedef's parameters, or a member of a union a pointer reaches.
- `ty.ffibox.sys.of_which.raw_ptr_in_sys.of_which.used` -- of those, the ones
  the crate's compiled code names: in a declaration, or as the type of any
  expression or binding in a body.
- `ty.ffibox.sys.of_which.raw_ptr_in_sys.of_which.wrapped` -- of those, the ones
  a cell's `CCell::C` names.
- `ty.ffibox.sys.as.borrowed.std.{pub,priv}` -- the same mentions as
  `wrapper.as`'s, of the raw struct a cell covers, its `CCell::C`: the C layout
  named where the wrapper could have been.
- `ty.ffibox.sys.as.borrowed.std.of_which.{field,fn_sig}.{pub,priv}` -- as above.
- `ty.ffibox.sys.as.borrowed.std.of_which.{self_in_ref_accessor,self_in_trait_impl}.{pub,priv}`
  -- as above.
- `ty.ffibox.sys.as.borrowed.std.of_which.self_in_trait_impl.of_which.ref_forming.{pub,priv}`
  -- as above.
- `ty.ffibox.sys.as.borrowed.ffibox.{pub,priv}` -- as above.
- `ty.ffibox.sys.as.borrowed.ffibox.of_which.{field,fn_sig}.{pub,priv}` -- as
  above.
- `ty.ffibox.sys.as.owned.std.{pub,priv}` -- as above.
- `ty.ffibox.sys.as.owned.std.of_which.{field,fn_sig}.{pub,priv}` -- as above.
- `ty.ffibox.sys.as.owned.ffibox.{pub,priv}` -- as above.
- `ty.ffibox.sys.as.owned.ffibox.of_which.{field,fn_sig}.{pub,priv}` -- as above.
- `ty.ffibox.sys.as.by_val.{pub,priv}` -- as above.
- `ty.ffibox.sys.as.by_val.of_which.{field,fn_sig}.{pub,priv}` -- as above.

### 1.3 `fn`

Every function the crate defines, the methods of its trait impls included
([analysis 9.4](analysis.md#94-functions-and-methods)).

- `fn.total.{pub,priv}` -- the denominator, emitted: every function with a body.
- `fn.total.of_which.macro.{pub,priv}` -- of those, the ones a macro wrote.
  Subtract for the hand-written total.
- `fn.safe.{pub,priv}` -- the safe ones.
- `fn.safe.of_which.with_unsafe.{pub,priv}` -- of those, the ones whose body
  contains an `unsafe` block: a safe fn discharging an obligation internally.
  Counted on the safe arm only ([2.5](#25-deliberate-asymmetries)).
- `fn.unsafe.{pub,priv}` -- the `unsafe fn`s. `fn.unsafe.pub` is the unsafe
  surface a consumer meets.
- `fn.unsafe.of_which.in_trait_impl.std.{pub,priv}` -- of those, the methods
  of a trait impl, whose `unsafe` the trait's declaration fixed and the impl
  cannot drop: here, a standard-library trait's.
- `fn.unsafe.of_which.in_trait_impl.local.{pub,priv}` -- a trait the crate
  declared itself, which put the `unsafe` there one level up.
- `fn.unsafe.of_which.in_trait_impl.ffibox.{pub,priv}` -- an ffibox contract,
  such as `CDrop::c_drop`.
- `fn.unsafe.of_which.in_trait_impl.other.{pub,priv}` -- any other crate's
  trait.
- `fn.unsafe.of_which.seam.{pub,priv}` -- the `unsafe fn`s `--seams` names,
  which adopt a raw pointer by design. A seam may also be a trait's method, so
  this overlaps `in_trait_impl`.
- `fn.unsafe.of_which.other.{pub,priv}` -- the residual: neither a trait
  impl's method nor a seam, the `unsafe` the crate chose with nothing
  requiring it.
- `fn.unsafe.of_which.outside_regions.{pub,priv}` -- the `unsafe fn`s outside
  every module `--regions` named: the unsafe API the crate did not confine
  (safety).
- `fn.extern_abi.{pub,priv}` -- the fns the crate defines with a foreign ABI
  (`extern "C"`), which C reaches by symbol or by fn pointer (soundness).
- `fn.extern_abi.of_which.exported.{pub,priv}` -- of those, the ones carrying a
  C symbol name (`#[no_mangle]`, `#[export_name]`).
- `fn.extern_abi.of_which.macro.{pub,priv}` -- the ones a macro wrote.
- `fn.extern_abi.of_which.catches_unwind.{pub,priv}` -- the ones whose body
  calls `std::panic::catch_unwind`, a fn `--barriers` named, or, under
  `--ffibox`, ffibox's `callback::barrier`: a panic stopped before it unwinds
  into C. The rest is read by subtracting (soundness).
- `fn.extern_abi.of_which.raw_ptr_sig.{pub,priv}` -- the ones whose signature
  holds a raw pointer.
- `fn.extern_abi.of_which.ffibox_sig.{pub,priv}` -- the ones whose signature
  holds an ffibox primitive, an owner or handle in place of a pointer.
- `fn.extern_abi.of_which.ffibox_macro.{pub,priv}` -- the ones an ffibox macro
  wrote, such as its `export_*!` lifecycle exports.
- `fn.sig.of_which.c_type.{arg,ret}.{pub,priv}` -- mentions of C's types in
  the signatures the crate chose, a trait impl's methods left out: C's scalar
  names (`c_int`, `c_char`, and `libc`'s), read from the signature as written
  since typeck erases them, and foreign-ABI fn pointers. What a consumer of a
  Rust API handles in C's terms (ergonomics).
- `fn.sig.of_which.result.ret.{pub,priv}` -- the fns, trait impls' methods
  left out, that return a `Result`: failure in Rust's vocabulary rather than
  C's status codes (idiomaticity).
- `fn.sig.of_which.ffibox.{arg,ret}.<primitive>.{pub,priv}` -- mentions of an
  ffibox primitive in a signature, by position and by primitive, the ones
  inside a `Result`, an `Option` or a reference included
  ([analysis 9.4](analysis.md#94-functions-and-methods)): whether the
  vocabulary actually crosses the interface.
- `fn.ffibox.sys.total` -- the fns the crates `--sys-crates` names declare,
  and those of the scanned crate's own modules it names as `crate::<path>`:
  the C functions the bindings expose, macro shims included. No `{pub,priv}`:
  they are another crate's.
- `fn.ffibox.sys.of_which.used` -- of those, the ones the crate's compiled code
  names, by calling one or coercing it to a pointer.
- `fn.ffibox.wrapper.{non_trait,other_trait}` -- the crate's fns annotated as
  wrappers of a C function: each `#[doc(alias)]` naming a fn of the `-sys`
  crates, once per alias and fn, so the variants a C function is forked into
  count once each. By where the annotated fn sits: a free fn or an inherent
  method (`non_trait`), or the method of a trait that is no ffibox policy
  (`other_trait`). No `{pub,priv}`, like `fn.ffibox.sys`.
- `fn.ffibox.wrapper.policy.<trait>` -- the method of an ffibox lifecycle
  policy, such as `CDrop::c_drop`, by trait: the allocate, release and clone
  groups of [ffibox.md](ffibox.md#1-the-vocabulary).
- `fn.ffibox.wrapper.of_which.unique` -- the distinct C functions they name.

### 1.4 `static`

The statics the crate defines; an `extern` block's declarations are C's.

- `static.total.{pub,priv}` -- every static the crate defines. Emitted, and the
  denominator its shares are read against.
- `static.of_which.mut.{pub,priv}` -- the `static mut`s: shared mutable state
  no borrow checks (soundness).
- `static.of_which.exported.{pub,priv}` -- the ones carrying a C symbol name,
  which C reads by that name (soundness).

### 1.5 `code`

The size of the crate and what its bodies do, as the denominators the rest is
read against.

- `code.loc.total` -- lines of code, from the compiled crate: the union of HIR
  definition spans, blanks and comments excluded, so items `cfg` removed are
  not in the denominator.
- `code.loc.unsafe` -- of those, the lines inside an `unsafe` block, filtered
  the same way so the two are comparable.
- `code.unsafe_block.total` -- `unsafe` blocks, however many lines each holds.
- `code.unsafe_block.of_which.ffi_export` -- of those, the ones inside a fn
  that is the C-ABI boundary: one with a foreign ABI or a C symbol name, or a
  closure inside one ([analysis 9.7](analysis.md#97-regions-and-the-c-abi-boundary)).
- `code.unsafe_block.of_which.region.<region>` -- the ones inside a module
  `--regions` named, or a module nested in one, by the innermost such module's
  name (safety).
- `code.unsafe_block.of_which.outside_regions` -- the ones inside none, another
  crate's macro expansions included: the unsafe the crate did not confine
  (safety).
- `code.unsafe_call.ffi` -- unsafe calls whose callee carries a foreign ABI:
  the real crossings, counted by the callee's type rather than by its
  declaration site, so calls through a stored function pointer are in
  ([analysis 10](analysis.md#10-calls)).
- `code.unsafe_call.rust` -- unsafe calls to a Rust-ABI function, the crate's
  own `unsafe fn`s and the standard library's unsafe constructors alike.
- `code.unsafe_call.intrinsic` -- unsafe calls to a compiler intrinsic,
  `transmute` among them.
- `code.fn_ptr.extern_abi.{local,foreign,other}` -- a fn with a foreign ABI
  turned into a fn pointer, by coercion or an `as` cast: how C is handed a
  callback. By what the fn is: one the crate defines (`local`), a C fn an
  `extern` block declares (`foreign`), or another crate's (`other`)
  (soundness).
- `code.fn_ptr.extern_abi.ffibox` -- under `--ffibox`, the calls that hand C an
  ffibox trampoline or release routine as a fn pointer (`trampoline`,
  `release_fn`, `release_fn_of`).
- `code.call.ffibox.{status,barrier}` -- under `--ffibox`, the calls to ffibox's
  status conventions, which turn a C status into a `Result`, and to its panic
  barrier. Read against `code.unsafe_call.ffi` (idiomaticity, soundness).
- `code.tests.loc.{total,unsafe}` -- the same two line counts for the test
  code, which no other counter includes
  ([analysis 9.6](analysis.md#96-test-code)).
- `code.tests.unsafe_block` -- `unsafe` blocks in the test code.
- `code.tests.fn` -- functions in the test code, including one generated
  harness `main` per test binary.

## 2. The shape of a record

### 2.1 Partitions and shares

A partition's children are disjoint and sum to it; an `of_which` node's
children are subsets that overlap and are never summed. `nest_ptr` derives
every partition `total` bottom-up and skips `of_which` when summing, so no sum
is written by the driver and none can disagree with its parts.

`ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which` is a share family: a type may implement both
`Drop` and `Clone`, so its arms overlap and only the record itself is a
population. An `of_which` node therefore carries no `total` of its own --
summing two shares is not a quantity -- while each share keeps the total of its
own `{pub,priv}` partition. A share may refine another share, and then it nests
under it: `fn_sig_trait_impl.of_which.ffibox.of_which.<trait>` is the ffibox
positions by trait.

One child is of another unit: `as` holds the mentions of the types its parent
counts -- `ty.ffibox.wrapper` is the cell types, `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as` the
places they are named -- so it is never summed into the parent either, while
it is a record with a total of its own, which its arms partition. So is
`ty.ffibox.wrapper.fields`, the fns annotated as field accessors on those
cells.

Where a residual is wanted it is emitted as a share named for it --
`ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.none`, `ty.total.of_which.no_trait` -- rather than
left for a reader to subtract.

### 2.2 Namespaces

Three kinds of node carry no derived `total`: an `of_which` node, as above; a
node that already carries an emitted one, which is how the denominators
`raw_ptr.total`, `ty.total` and `code.loc.total` survive a derivation that
would otherwise take their name; and a NAMESPACE, a node whose children are
families rather than the parts of one quantity.

A top-level prefix is always a namespace -- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg` counts
signature positions and `raw_ptr.deref` counts body sites, so their sum means
nothing -- and four are namespaces a level down. `ty.ffibox` holds two type
counts, the cells (`wrapper`) and the `-sys` crates' types (`sys`), each with
its mentions under `as`. `code.tests` holds four separate
measurements of the test build: its lines, its unsafe lines -- a subset of them
-- its unsafe blocks and its fns; their sum read 103840 on libgit2-bindings, a
figure with no unit at all. `fn.sig` holds what a signature carries, in
mentions -- a fn taking two `CBox` is two of them -- so it is a share of no
count of fns, and `fn.total` beside it is the denominator a reader divides by.
Its own arms do carry totals: `fn.sig.of_which.ffibox` is `arg` plus `ret`,
which are disjoint. `fn.ffibox` holds two fn counts as `ty.ffibox` holds two
type counts: the crate's annotated wrappers (`wrapper`) and the `-sys` crates'
fns (`sys`).

`nest_ptr` declares them in `NAMESPACES` rather than inferring them, since no
shape distinguishes a namespace from a partition: `raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg`'s
`{safe,unsafe}` children are records with their own totals too, and summing
those is exactly right.

### 2.3 Zero, and absent

Every counter the invocation's flags turn on is in the document, at `0` when
it never fired. A reader of one document cannot tell an absent counter from
one the schema does not have -- no `owned.std` under `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as`
could mean "no cell is held in a std collection" or "that arm was never
written" --
and the schema is too long to hold in the head, so the driver registers every
path it can emit before the passes run and they count up from there.

What is absent is what the flags did not turn on, which is a different
statement and a deliberate one: the ffibox arms without `--ffibox`, and the
`of_which.seam` shares without `--seams`. A `0` there would say the scan
looked and found none, when it did not look.

The registry is in the driver, beside the passes, and it iterates the same
vocabulary lists they do, so the trait and primitive arms cannot drift from
it. `RegistryTests` reads the registry off a scan of
`tests/fixtures/empty/` -- a crate with nothing in it, whose every counter is
therefore 0 -- and holds the other fixtures' fired counters to it.

### 2.4 The order of a record

A record's children are written in a declared order, most salient first: the
record's own `total`, then the splits it is cut by (`unsafe` before `safe`,
`pub` before `priv`), then its families, then its shares and arms, and
`of_which` last, since a share is read against the partition it cuts across.
The prefixes come in this document's order: `raw_ptr`, `ty`, `fn`, `code`.

The driver emits a sorted map, so the alternative is alphabetical: `fn` would
read `{safe, sig, total, unsafe}`, with the denominator in the middle.

A name the order does not hold comes after every name it does, alphabetically.
That is where the primitive arms land -- `CArc`, `CBorrowedPtr`, `CBox` -- so a
primitive added to ffibox needs no change to the order and still reads
predictably. The trait arms are declared, in the order
[`ffibox.md`](ffibox.md) gives the vocabulary, so a breakdown by trait reads as
the lifecycle it describes rather than alphabetically.
`measure.KEY_ORDER` is one table for every level, since a name that earns an
early rank in one record earns it in the others: `unsafe` is early as
`fn.unsafe`, as `code.loc.unsafe` and as the unsafe trait impls. `fn` is the
one name it cannot place for every record, being a prefix as well as one of
`code.tests`'s measurements, so it is ranked for the latter. A type count's
`as` comes after its `of_which`, since the mentions are read once the types
are.

### 2.5 Deliberate asymmetries

A split that is not carried where a reader might expect it, and why.

`ty.impl_trait.of_which.ffibox.{layout,policy}.of_which.<trait>` splits
`{handwritten,macro}` but not `{pub,priv}`: whether a generator was used does
not vary with visibility, and the split would cost a cell per trait for
nothing.

`raw_ptr.fn_sig_trait_impl.of_which.ffibox.of_which.<trait>` splits by neither:
a trait method's safety and visibility are the trait declaration's, one
spelling dictating every impl, so the split would restate the parent cell by
cell. The parent `ffibox` arm carries both, since the mix of traits a crate
implements does move them.

`fn.safe.of_which.with_unsafe` is counted on the safe arm only. With
`unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn` denied, every `unsafe fn` doing anything raw has a
block by construction, so counting it there would measure the lint.

`raw_ptr.fn_sig_trait_impl` carries no direction, while `fn_sig_arg` and
`fn_sig_ret` are separate counters: the direction says what the crate chose to
do with the pointer, and in a trait impl it chose neither.

## 3. Building a report

A report is leaves divided and subtracted, named by their paths. Three rules
make the arithmetic sound:

- a partition may be summed, an `of_which` may not, and an `as` never with the
  types above it. Two shares of one record overlap, so
  `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.impl_drop + impl_clone` is not a quantity, while
  `pub + priv` is the record;
- a rate stays inside one record, or between a record and the denominator
  emitted for it: `fn.unsafe.pub / fn.total.pub`, `code.loc.unsafe /
  code.loc.total`, `ty.storing_raw_ptr.pub / ty.total.pub`. Dividing across
  prefixes mixes grains -- signature positions by lines of code says nothing;
- a share is read against the record it cuts, and the remainder is a
  subtraction: `wrapper.as.borrowed.std.pub` less its two sanctioned shares is
  the convention's unsanctioned surface.

### 3.1 The readings worth taking

Each reading below names the leaves it is made of. The figures are not here: a
reading of one crate is in [`analysis.md`](analysis.md), where it is the
evidence for a rule, and a reading of several is in
[`examples/README.md`](../examples/README.md), where three real documents are
tabulated side by side. A figure copied into this document would be a second
copy to keep current, and the counters are what this document is for.

**How much of the bindings has a cell.** Under `--ffibox` with the `-sys`
crates named, `ty.ffibox.sys.of_which.raw_ptr_in_sys.of_which.wrapped` against
`raw_ptr_in_sys` is the share of the C types the bindings hand around by pointer
that the crate has given a cell, and `used` against it the share the crate
touches at all, so the gap between the two shares is the C it touches
without a cell ([ffibox.md](ffibox.md#8-where-the-declarations-mention-a-cell)). Against `ty.ffibox.sys.total` it reads low by
construction, since a by-value struct needs no cell.

**How much of the C functions has a wrapper.** Under `--ffibox` with the
`-sys` crates named, `fn.ffibox.wrapper.of_which.unique` against
`fn.ffibox.sys.total` is the share of the C functions the bindings declare
that the crate annotates a wrapper for, and `fn.ffibox.sys.of_which.used`
against it the share it calls at all. The annotation is the only record of
what a wrapper wraps, so an unannotated wrapper reads as none; the alias is
the one the Crustify conventions require. `fn.ffibox.wrapper.total` against
`unique` is how many variants a wrapped function was forked into on average.

**Which `unsafe fn`s nothing required.** `fn.unsafe.of_which.other` is the
unsafe surface the crate chose: no trait declared the method unsafe and no
seam adopts a pointer through it. Read it against `fn.unsafe`, and its `pub`
leaf against `fn.unsafe.pub`, rather than subtracting `in_trait_impl` and
`seam`, which overlap.

**What a consumer meets without writing `unsafe`.**
`raw_ptr.total.safe.pub` is the raw pointers on the safe public interface,
`fn.unsafe.pub` against `fn.total.pub` the public unsafe surface, and
`raw_ptr.field.pub` the pointers a public field hands over with no `unsafe` at
all.

**How much unsafe, and where it sits.** `code.loc.unsafe / code.loc.total` is
the density and `code.unsafe_block.total` the number of blocks; read both,
since folding small blocks into large ones moves one and not the other.
`code.unsafe_block.of_which.ffi_export` subtracts the gateways a port campaign
generated, and the `code.unsafe_call` arms say what the unsafe is for: `ffi`
is the boundary, `rust` is the standard library's constructors and the crate's
own helpers, `intrinsic` is `transmute` and its siblings.

**What the crate wrote, as opposed to what a macro did.** Subtract
`fn.total.of_which.macro` from `fn.total`, and
`ty.impl_trait.of_which.derived` from `ty.impl_trait`. A comparison of two
crates without those shares is partly a comparison of how much boilerplate
each spells.

**What the crate declares about the pointers it manages.**
`ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.none` against `ty.storing_raw_ptr` is the types
that hold a pointer and say nothing about it. The other shares say what the
rest declared -- `impl_drop`, `impl_clone`, `ffibox` -- and `pub_field` is the
opposite of a declaration.

**Whether a convention is kept.** Under `--ffibox`,
`ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.borrowed.std` less `self_in_ref_accessor` and
`self_in_trait_impl` is the bare `&Foo` surface the convention says should be a
handle. `as.owned.std` and `as.by_val` against `as.owned.ffibox` say how much
of a cell's storage the crate holds itself rather than through ffibox's
owners. `ty.ffibox.wrapper.of_which.no_seam_trait` is the cells a generic
handle has to special-case, and `fn.sig.of_which.ffibox` whether the
vocabulary reaches the interface at all.

**What the trait impls do.** `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std`'s arms say which of
the crate's adopted traits act on what it wraps: `drop` and `clone` run its
lifecycle, `send` and `sync` are claims about threads, `ref_forming` can hand
out a reference to it. Under `--ffibox`, `ty.impl_trait.of_which.ffibox`'s
`layout` and `policy` say how much of the convention is the cells' layout and
how much their lifecycle.

**Whose shape the pointers in trait impls are.** `fn_sig_trait_impl` is read
through its `of_which` arms, never bare: one crate's are a convention's
lifecycle strategies, another's its own private helpers, a third's one local
conversion trait, and the bare figure is the same for all three.

**The test code, beside the library and never added to it.**
`code.tests.loc.total` against `code.loc.total` is how much of the tree is
tests, and the `code.tests` arms are the only counters that include them.

A report of several crates is a table of leaves, one row per crate, with the
denominator beside every share.

### 3.2 What a comparison requires

The document is a pure function of the source tree under a fixed scanner, so
two figures are comparable only when the scanner and the flags match: the
ffimap commit, the toolchain, `--sys-crates` (which decides what
`ty.storing_raw_ptr` admits), `--seams` (which decides what the `seam` shares
and `casted_to.local_seam` can see) and any framework the crate is built on.
The `scanner` and `sys_crates` fields carry all of it, which is why they are in
the document rather than beside it. `scanner.ffimap` names one scanner only as
a commit, bare or with the hash of its uncommitted changes: a package version
is what every copy outside a checkout of its own records, so `ffimap diff`
reports two such documents as under scanners not known to be the same
([analysis 1](analysis.md#1-determinism-and-what-it-rests-on)).

A counter added or a rule corrected moves figures too. The ones already known
to be incomparable across versions are named in
[analysis 12](analysis.md#12-what-the-analysis-cannot-see).

### 3.3 No target values

ffimap has none, and this is the place that says so. Absolute counts are not
comparable across crates of different size, and lower is not automatically
better: a wrapper over C must contain unsafe, and folding 600 small audited
blocks into 200 large ones improves the number while making the crate worse.
A reader who wants a rate divides the leaves it names.

Finding what is worth looking at is the opposite kind of work, and belongs to
a reviewer who reads the code, forms suspicions and defends them. `none` and
`no_seam_trait` name an absence, not a defect.

content.content:
# API stability per C item

`ffimap api` measures a promise a C-to-Rust migration makes to its Rust
consumers: once a C item has a safe Rust API, wrapping it, porting it and its
later stages leave that API alone. It reads the crate's rustdoc JSON, finds the
Rust items that stand in for each C item through their anchors, and records
their consumer-facing surface twice: raw, as the signatures stand, and as the
**contract** a consumer may rely on whatever form a handle or an owner takes.
Two such records, one at the item's first landing and one after a later
landing, say whether the contract was kept, extended or changed. This document is what the two documents hold and every
rule behind them. The scan's counters are [`schema.md`](schema.md)'s and have
nothing to do with it.

## 1. Input

```sh
cargo +nightly-2026-10-07 rustdoc -p CRATE --lib -- -Z unstable-options --output-format json
(cd ffibox && cargo +nightly-2026-10-07 rustdoc --lib -- -Z unstable-options \
    --output-format json --document-private-items)
ffimap api extract target/doc/CRATE.json --dep ffibox/target/doc/ffibox.json > before.json
```

`--dep` gives the rustdoc JSON of a crate the measured one depends on, and is
repeatable. The contracts of handles and owners that are aliases into ffibox
(`CBox`, `CArc`, `CVal`, …) need ffibox's, since the reborrows and trait impls
those forms inherit live there; it is made with `--document-private-items`
because the bounds rustdoc synthesises for ffibox's auto-trait impls name its
private fields' types. Without it those contracts are unresolved, as section 6
describes. The measure is pure Python over the JSON. It does not use the driver, so the
crate need not build on the driver's nightly, only document on one whose JSON
format it reads.

Rustdoc's JSON is unstable: each nightly writes a `format_version`, and the
shape moves with it. `ffimap api` reads **format 61**, which
nightly-2026-10-07 (the driver's pin) and nightly-2026-10-08 emit, and refuses
any other with an error naming the version it found. Support for a new format
is added by checking the fields `src/ffimap/rustdoc.py` reads against it and
adding it to `FORMAT_VERSIONS`.

## 2. C items and their stand-ins

A C item is keyed by its anchor's `<kind>::<path>`: `fn::git_mailmap_new`,
`st::git_mailmap`, `fld::git_buf.ptr`. An anchor is a doc-comment line of its
own, exactly ``Wraps `<kind>::<path>` `` or ``Replaces `<kind>::<path>` ``,
where the path is names separated by dots and a `fld` path names a member. Every
public item of the crate that carries one is a **stand-in** of that C item, and
an item carrying several (the accessor of two members) is a stand-in of each.

What the extract reports about the anchors themselves, under `anchors`:

- `malformed`: a line that tries to be an anchor and is not one -- the verb and
  a `kind::` path inside a sentence, with a trailing period, without backticks,
  or with a path that is not names. It keys nothing.
- `unknown_kinds`: anchors whose kind is not one of the convention's (`fn`,
  `st`, `un`, `enm`, `fnp`, `tdf`, `fld`, `glb`, `mac`), counted by kind. They
  are keyed as written.
- `without_alias`: anchors on an item with no `#[doc(alias)]` naming the
  anchor's path. An item whose own name is the anchor's path is left out:

matched with the next's:

| item | locator |
|---|---|
| a free item | its canonical path |
| an item of an inherent impl | `Ty::name` |
| an item of a trait impl | `<Ty as Trait<Args>>::name` |
| a trait's item, a variant, a field | its owner's locator `::name` |

in order among equals. An item defined in a private module and re-exported from
its parent is named by the parent's path, and a port that moves the definition
into the parent changes nothing. An item of another crate is named by its
definition's path in the `paths` table, `ffibox::refs::CBox` for instance,

source wrote, so an import or a reordering of the source gives the same bytes.

trait's, recorded where the trait is.

The types a consumer reaches a C type through -- `FooRef`, `FooMut`, `FooBox`,

content.content:
# Goals

This file states what Crustify is for and how it evolves. Every change to Crustify is judged
against these goals, whether it changes its skills, its agents or its tools.

A rule that serves none of these goals is removed. Where two goals are in tension, they are
weighed for the case at hand, and the weighing is stated.

The goals evolve too, from the same evidence as everything else:

- a goal the campaigns keep missing;
- a goal no decision ever cites;
- two goals that keep conflicting the same way; or
- a well-founded change that none of the goals serves.

A change to the goals is proposed as Crustify's `evolution` skill describes. It lands only
with the user's approval.

Each goal names its *fitness*: what a campaign measures to tell how far the goal is met. Each
thing measured is a *measure*. A measure is read from one of two sources, and no run is made
only to take it:

- what the campaign's runs produce anyway: the dashboard, the review reports, the gates and
  the plan; or
- a rerun the campaign's reviews already make.

A *tier* is one of the checks that code meets one after another. An *escape* is a defect
caught by a later tier than the one that read the code first. Later tiers include:

- a module pass after a wave's review;
- a switch;
- a revisit; and
- a ship point's gates.

Worse work could improve some measures. Such a measure is *paired* with the measure that
catches the worse work, which is its *pair*, and neither is read alone. When there are more
escapes, fewer findings is no gain. When the work is redone, cheaper work is no gain.

Some measures are held by no artifact yet. Such a measure is marked **Not taken yet**. Until
it is taken, what it measures is judged, not measured.

Under each goal, **Measure** states a measure, **Paired with** names its pair, and **Not
taken yet** names what no artifact holds yet.

## 2. Equivalence

The Rust keeps the C's specified behaviour, not its bugs. The specified behaviour is what
the C's documentation, tests and consumers rely on.

- **Measure.**
  - The target's own tests passing over the Rust at each switch, against their recorded
    baseline.
  - The inputs and states on which the Rust is compared with the C it replaces, with no
    difference left unexplained.
  - The differences made on purpose, each documented and held by a test.
- **Paired with** the differences found after the comparison ended. They are found by a
  review, at a switch, or by a consumer.
- **Not taken yet.** The inputs compared and the deliberate differences, as figures. Each
  run's notes alone hold them.

## 3. Idiomatic Rust
## 5. Verification

What the agents produce is machine-checked wherever it can be, rather than left to an
agent's judgement. It is checked by types, lints, sanitizers, Miri, schemas, deterministic
tools and compile-time assertions.

- **Measure.** The line coverage of the ported Rust.
- **Paired with** the share of deliberate faults that the ported Rust's tests catch, since
  code that runs is not code that is checked.
- **Paired with** the gate results that a run reported and that its landed tree does not
  reproduce. A review files these gate results among its reports.
- **Not taken yet.**
  - the seeded faults, which are taken only where a review happens to seed them;
  - the region coverage of the ported Rust; and
  - the states and transitions the tests reach.
  <!-- TODO: seeding faults is not a step of any stage yet. -->

## 6. Maintainability

# A module pass seeds faults in the ported code before the switch retires its equivalence tests

Status: `open`.

## Signal

A landed change that did not hold. The record's row of `equiv-tests-without-c` (crustify
`7da3744`) watches for "a review or test-adequacy finding of behaviour only a retired equivalence
test checked". This pass found such behaviour before the retirement, and only by seeding faults:
`porting-workflow` keeps what the retiring equivalence tests established "by its unit tests", and
`reviewing`'s Test adequacy objective names "assertions too weak to fail when the code is wrong",
but neither says how a module pass tells, and coverage, the one measure the skills give, cannot:
the ported function runs every line on every call.

It is also a measure `GOALS.md` names and no stage takes: Verification's pair, "the share of
deliberate faults that the ported Rust's tests catch", **Not taken yet** ("the seeded faults,
which are taken only where a review happens to seed them"), with the TODO "seeding faults is not
a step of any stage yet".

## Evidence

- `wave-221/batch-3/run-1`, `src/util/hash/sha1dc/ubc_check.c`'s module pass. `ubc_check`, a
  statement-for-statement port of 470 lines of generated conditions, is covered to 100% of its
  lines and regions (`wave-221/batch-1`'s figures). The pass seeded 558 faults in it, one per
  site: each word index moved by one (312), each bit of a `1 << k` moved by one (118), each
  `== 0`/`!= 0` inverted (128), each built as its own binary with the function's unit-test
  checks, and each compared with the unmutated function over 2^17 seeded blocks and every one-bit
  change of a block selecting each vector, which told all 558 apart from the original. The
  module's `unit_pub` tests caught 406 and let 152 through (27%); its `equiv` tests, which compare
  with the C and retire at the switch, caught the 8 hand-made mutants of the same kinds that the
  pass first built in the crate, the one `unit_pub` missed among them. Two `unit_pub` tests the
  pass added (`ubc_check_of_each_one_bit_change_of_a_witness_is_cs` and
  `ubc_check_of_many_seeded_blocks_folds_as_c_does`, their expected values computed by the C)
  catch all 558.
- The same pass seeded one fault in the gateway, an export that writes a zero mask: the gateway's
  own test, the only test of the export that stays after the switch, passed it, every one of its
  35 blocks giving a zero mask; the relinked `util_tests`' `sha1::detect_collision_attack` failed
  it.
- `wave-197/batch-1/run-1` (`deps/llhttp/http.c`) and `wave-194/batch-7/run-1`
  (`deps/llhttp/api.c`), the module passes before those switches, mapped each retiring
  equivalence test to the unit tests that keep it by reading (http.c's run dir's
  `equiv-retirement.md`), and added unit tests where the reading found none; neither seeded a
  fault, so neither could tell an assertion too weak to fail.

## Goal

Verification: its pair, the share of seeded faults the ported Rust's tests catch, taken at the
tier where it matters most, the last before the comparison with the C ends. And Equivalence:
"the differences found after the comparison ended", which a fault the unit tests let through
becomes once a later change makes it.

## Destination

The spec, both texts protected (`skills/verification/**`), so the change waits for the user:

- `reviewing`, Test adequacy (`test-adequacy`): in a module pass before a switch, the ported
  code's faults are seeded, and the share the tests that outlive the C catch is measured, with the
  module's equivalence tests telling a fault apart from an equivalent rewrite; a gap is filled with
  tests, as now, until they catch what the equivalence tests catch.
- `testing-builds`, Coverage: the share beside the coverage figures, as the measure that coverage
  is paired with.

A script beside `testing-builds` that seeds a function's faults by kind and runs a test filter
over each would make the step deterministic; this pass's was a scratch harness over a copy of the
function, which is not one.

## Change

Not made. One paragraph in `reviewing`'s Test adequacy: "A module pass before its module's switch
seeds faults in the module's ported functions, one per site of a kind it names (an index, a
constant, a comparison or an operator changed), and runs over each the tests that outlive the C,
its unit and UB tests and its gateway's, with the module's equivalence tests run over the same
faults to set aside those that change nothing. The faults the equivalence tests catch and the
others let through are gaps, filled as this objective fills any. The pass records the faults
seeded and the share caught, before and after." And one line in `testing-builds`' Coverage naming
that share as the figure coverage is read beside.

## Record

| change | from | landed as | signal answered | recurrence signal | status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| a module pass seeds faults in the ported code before its switch, and fills the gaps the unit tests leave against the retiring equivalence tests | `libgit2-crustify`, `module-pass-seeds-faults-before-the-switch` | — | a module whose unit tests ran every line of its port let 27% of its seeded faults through, which only its equivalence tests, retired at the switch, caught | a finding, after a switch, of behaviour that a fault seeded at the module pass would have shown and the unit tests do not check | watched |

# A port batch runs its module's tests with its exports linked in place of its C

Status: `open`.

## Signal

One procedure repeated by hand, which no gate runs. `testing-gates`' Regressions section
has a `port` batch check and lint the safe crate with its module's export feature on,
"which compiles the module's gateway without linking it", and compare each export's
signature with its raw binding. Nothing runs the gateway before the module's switch: every
gate builds with the feature off, and the `testing` skill puts an export's tests "with the
stage that removes the form", which compile only under the feature. A gateway that
compiles, and has C's signature, but writes the wrong out-parameter, reads past its size or
mishandles a NULL, passes every gate until the switch rebuilds the variants, when the C
tests that remain are the first to call it.

## Evidence

- `wave-229/batch-0/run-1` (`src/util/utf8.c`, the crate's first gateway) ran, "as a
  scratch check, not a gate", its tests with the exports linked in place of the archive's
  `utf8.o` (its dashboard notes).
- `wave-229/batch-1/run-1`, its module pass, did it again, by hand: a private build dir under
  `crustify/tmp/` whose entries link to the variant's, but for a copy of its static archive
  without the module's objects (`ar d libcrustify.a utf8.c.o`), named by
  `CRUSTIFY_BUILD_DIR`; then `cargo-variant.sh <variant> test --workspace --features
  ffi-export-src-util-utf8-c` on `plain` and `asan-ubsan`, which passed but for the known
  nightly failures, `nm` showing no `utf8proc_utf8class` and `next_hfs_char` calling Rust.
  It also relinked the variant's C test executables (`libgit2_tests`, `util_tests`) from
  their `build.ninja` edges, without `src/util/CMakeFiles/util.dir/utf8.c.o` and with the
  crate built as a `staticlib` with the feature on: `-sutf8`, and `-spath -sdiff -sindex
  -scheckout -srefs`, gave the stock binaries' results (825 passed, 22 skipped). A
  `util_tests` input list holds two `utf8.c.o`, the module's and its C test's, so removing
  by file name alone would drop the test: the procedure must name the object's path.
- The module pass added the gateway's own `unit_priv` tests, which compile only under the
  feature, and ran them by hand with it on, under Miri too.
- `wave-186/batch-5/run-1` and `wave-186/batch-6/run-1` (`git2/src/cli/opt.c`) ran the
  module's `equiv` tests the same way, by hand, against a copy of the archive without
  `opt.c.o`; those tests compare the C with the Rust, so with the exports linked they compare
  the exports with the native API, and they are retired with the C at the switch.
- `wave-186/batch-7/run-1`, the module pass, found the gateway with no test of its own and two
  defects that only the export's callers reach. Its gateway tests, written after `main.c`,
  `cmd_hash_object.c` and `common.c`, ran with the feature on against the private build and
  under Miri, where the feature also compiles: Miri reported
  `ub_export/args-slot-handed-to-c-through-a-dead-borrow`, a `char **` the export stored for C
  that a later unique reborrow invalidated, which no gate could reach, since every gate builds
  with the feature off. The module's remaining C is an executable, the CLI, which no C test
  runs (`modules.json`'s `tests` is empty, and no suite under `c/tests` reaches `src/cli`), so
  the switch's C-test gate checks nothing of these exports. The pass relinked the variant's
  `git2` from its `build.ninja` edge, without `src/cli/CMakeFiles/git2_cli.dir/opt.c.o` and
  with the crate built as a `staticlib` with the feature on, and ran it and the stock `git2`
  over 66 command lines in scratch repositories: 62 alike, the 4 others the parser's recorded
  departures from the C. The procedure is recorded for this target as a lesson
  (`crustify/LESSONS.md`, "A `git2` module's exports are checked through the CLI").

- `wave-194/batch-4/run-1` (`deps/llhttp/api.c`, its last `port` batch) ran it by hand again,
  as its task message asked, on `plain` and `asan-ubsan`: private build dirs under
  `crustify/tmp/linkcheck/<variant>` linking to the variant's entries, with a copy of
  `libcrustify.a` less `api.c.o` (211 objects), named by `CRUSTIFY_BUILD_DIR`, and the tests
  run with `--features ffi-export-deps-llhttp-api-c`. Two things the procedure must say came
  out of it. First, not every test binary can link: the module's `equiv` binary calls 19 of
  api.c's functions that no remaining C calls and that therefore have no export
  (`llhttp_get_type`, the lenient setters, `llhttp_reset`, …), so it fails to link
  (`undefined symbol`), by design, since it compares with that C; the check runs the other
  binaries and the doctests, and the undefined symbols of `equiv` are the list of the module's
  unexported functions, every one of which should be api.c's own. Second, a test outside
  `equiv` that calls such a function through its raw binding fails to link too, and would
  fail at the switch: `ub_unsafe`'s llhttp fixtures called `llhttp_settings_init`, which the
  batch replaced with the zeroed table it makes. The rest passed (`lib` 858 with the gateway's
  six tests, `ub_safe` 785, `ub_unsafe` 134, `unit_pub` 156, doctests 92 and 387; under
  ASan+UBSan the same but for the known nightly `compile_fail` snapshots and `CommitBuilder`
  doctest), `nm` showing the exports defined and api.c's other symbols absent.

- `wave-194/batch-7/run-1`, api.c's module pass, found that leaving `equiv` out of the check
  is itself a gap. `equiv` is one binary for every module, and `llhttp.c`'s equivalence
  tests (`tests/equiv/deps/llhttp/llhttp.rs`), which stay, also called 10 of api.c's
  unexported functions, so retiring api.c's own equivalence file at the switch would still
  have left `equiv` unlinked
  (`misc/llhttp-equiv-tests-call-api-c-functions-without-exports`). `rust-lld` lists only
  20 undefined symbols by default, so the full list needs its `--error-limit=0`. The
  pass moved those tests into api.c's file, then ran the check over a scratch tree with that
  file retired, as the switch will: `equiv` linked, 532 passing on `plain`, ASan+UBSan and
  TSan. So the check must link `equiv` too, with only the module's own equivalence files
  retired, and fail on any undefined symbol it references from another module's file.

- `wave-197/batch-0/run-1` (`deps/llhttp/http.c`, its whole `port`) ran the check by hand
  again, as its task message asked, on `plain` and `asan-ubsan`, over a scratch tree with its
  own equivalence file retired: every binary linked, `equiv` included (532), and passed but
  for the known nightly failures under ASan+UBSan. Removing the module's object by name would
  have removed the wrong one: the archive holds two `http.c.o` members,
  `src/libgit2/transports/http.c`'s (the 154th) and `deps/llhttp/http.c`'s (the 168th), and
  `ar d libcrustify.a http.c.o` deletes the first; the batch used `ar dN 2` and checked with
  `nm` that the member left defines `git_smart_subtransport_http`. So the script must take
  the module's objects by their `build.ninja` paths, as the `util_tests` evidence above found
  for a link's inputs, and pick an archive member by position, never by its base name alone.
  It also relinked the variants' `git2` and `libgit2_tests` from their `build.ninja` edges,
  without `deps/llhttp/CMakeFiles/llhttp.dir/http.c.o` and with the crate's static library
  built with the feature on, and ran `crustify/scripts/http-gate.sh` over them on `plain`,
  `asan-ubsan` and `coverage`, the module's only C callers being the HTTP client and
  `llhttp.c`, which no offline C test reaches.

- `wave-221/batch-1/run-1` (`src/util/hash/sha1dc/ubc_check.c`, its whole `port`, a function
  and a global, `ubc_check` and `sha1_dvs`, both for `sha1.c`) ran the check by hand, on
  `plain`, with no private archive: every external symbol of `ubc_check.o` is exported (the
  rest is `static`), so the linker resolves them all from the Rust and never pulls the
  archive member; `nm` on the `equiv` binary with the feature on shows one `sha1_dvs`, `R`,
  and none of the TU's `static const` bit constants, which it shows with the feature off.

# Where an exported global's storage is defined while its export feature is off

Status: `open`.

## Signal

A rule an agent had to work out by hand that a skill should state. `porting-symbols`'
Globals section has a ported global's storage held by Rust "from its port, beside its
module's C, which keeps its own copy until the switch; from then on the Rust's is the only
one", and a global the remaining C accesses "is exported, as a function is". The
conventions' Exports and Export features sections put every export in the module's
`ffi_export` gateway, compiled only under the export feature, which stays off until the
switch, and put every `#[unsafe(…)]` attribute in a region. For a function, the native
function and its export are two items, so the native one compiles with the feature off and
the export calls it. A global's export is its storage: the symbol C reads is the static
itself. With the feature off, the native API needs the storage, which the gateway cannot
hold; with it on, a second static in the gateway would make two Rust copies, against "the
Rust's is the only one"; and `#[unsafe(no_mangle)]` or `#[unsafe(export_name)]` on the
native static, under a `cfg_attr`, would put unsafe code outside the regions. No skill says
which of these a port takes, and the crate held no exported global to follow: the
switched modules' exports are all functions.

## Evidence

`wave-221/batch-1/run-1` (`src/util/hash/sha1dc/ubc_check.c`), whose table `sha1_dvs`
`sha1.c`'s C reads (`sha1_process`) and keeps reading through the export once the module
switches, since `sha1.c` stays C past the campaign's first ship point. The batch defined
the table's data once, as a private `const DVS`, and its storage under the two exclusive
configurations:

```rust
#[cfg(not(feature = "ffi-export-src-util-hash-sha1dc-ubc-check-c"))]
pub static SHA1_DVS: [DvInfo; DV_COUNT] = DVS;

#[cfg(feature = "ffi-export-src-util-hash-sha1dc-ubc-check-c")]
pub use self::ffi_export::sha1_dvs as SHA1_DVS;

// in `mod ffi_export`:
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub static sha1_dvs: [DvInfo; DV_COUNT] = DVS;
```

so that each build holds one Rust copy, which the native API names by its Rust name in
both, and the remaining C reads that copy once the feature is on. With the feature on, the
test binaries link it in place of the archive's `ubc_check.c.o`: `nm` shows one `sha1_dvs`,
`R`, and none of the TU's `static const` bit constants, and a gateway `unit_priv` test
checks that `&raw const sha1_dvs` and `&raw const SHA1_DVS` are one address.
`non_upper_case_globals`, which the workspace denies, exempts a `#[no_mangle]` static, and
`build.rs`'s `exported_name` reads the `pub static sha1_dvs` line as an export. At the
switch, deleting the feature removes the `cfg(not(…))` static and the `cfg` of the
re-export, and the storage stays the gateway's until the global's `port/unexport` moves it
back to the native code.

## Goal

Consistency (the same case written the same way in every module) and Interoperability
(one copy of each global, which the remaining C and the Rust share). Fitness: a review
finding of an exported global held twice, or of its export outside the gateway, which this
rule prevents.

## Destination

The spec: `porting-symbols`' Globals section, which the translator's role evolves; the
conventions' Exports section names it.

## Change

Not made yet, pending review of the pattern on this batch's module pass. One paragraph in
`porting-symbols`' Globals section, after "is exported, as a function is": the global's
data is one constant; while its export feature is off, the native static holds it under
`cfg(not(feature))`; under the feature, the gateway's `#[unsafe(no_mangle)]` static, under
the C name, is the storage, and the module re-exports it under the native name, so that
each build has one copy and the API's path does not change; the switch removes the native
static and the re-export's `cfg`; its `port/unexport` moves the storage back to the native
code. And a sentence in `porting-workflow`'s Builds section's first step, naming the
re-export among the mentions of the feature the switch rewrites.
